The PM promotes and actively encourages coherency, quality assurance and crosspollination across field teams.

The PM will provide leadership for Team Leaders in close liaison with the HoP and will work directly with the Protection Advisor and Programme Development Team.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Programme Management**

- Responsible for the overall planning and effective delivery of the project(s) in areas of implementation through the application of Unarmed Civilian Protection approach.
- Provide technical advice and oversight for the field teams implementing violence reduction projects, either directly or through team leaders in field sites.
- Together with the SPM, guide teams in strategic planning, development of work plans and adapting implementation to address emerging protection needs and contextual or operational challenges.
- Provide oversight, monitoring and review of Salesforce reporting and contribute to internal reporting upon request (including context, programming, staffing and welfare). Highlight to SMT key points from Salesforce Activity Reporting.
- The PM will support field teams and serve as interlocutor with Management and the Programme Development team if programming has to be adapted to address dynamic contextual realities and/or if changing circumstances renders the project objectives irrelevant or impossible.
- Work very closely with MEL team to ensure the effective implementation of the monitoring, evaluation, and learning strategy of program in each of the program locations.
- Engage in direct programme implementation as needed, participate in integrated capacities and needs assessments and emergency response if needed. This may include direct support with in-house and partner technical trainings. Stand in as Acting Team Leader when necessary.
- Contribute to broader country programme strategy development together with the rest of the Programme and Management team.
- Participate in grant inception process with programme development, finance and operations and then lead grant inception process with field teams in partnership with Programme Development department.
- When requested, contribute to donor reporting for area of operations.
- When requested, support assessments and start-up in new areas of implementation.

**Representation and Advocacy**

- Represent NP in coordination and advocacy fora where appropriate and needed, including on issue-based advocacy in the South of Ukraine.
- Represent NP at the sub-national level (with local authorities in field locations) when Team Leaders request senior support.
- Provide guidance and direct support on access related negotiations in areas of operation as needed in close coordination with the SSA and HoM.
- In collaboration with the Programme Development team, represent NP in the South of Ukraine to donors, engaging in proactive communication to keep donors updated on the progress of the project and the evolving conflict and protection context.
- Represent NP in the South of Ukraine during donor visits to areas of operation and planning donor visits together with the Programme Development team and will whenever possible, accompany the donor on field visits.

**Financial & Operational Management**

- Supervise and ensure that teams comply with their internal and external reporting requirements.
- Support FPO and TL with field level budget management including coding of field level expenses in accordance with approved project budgets.
- Work directly with TLs to prepare monthly site forecasting and monthly reporting of actuals against forecasts and flag under/overspends and offer corrective measures.
- In coordination with SPM, establish site spending strategies to ensure best use of available funds as well as allocating team attention towards necessary budget line spending.
- Serve as interlocutor between field teams and programme support departments (HR, Finance and Operations), ensuring that the needs of field teams are met and that field teams are fully aware of what is happening operationally in the Country Office as it relates to their sites.

**Personnel Management**

- Serve as Line Manager for Team Leaders.
- Facilitate strong staff morale and positive working environment using and practicing the NP values as central guidance.
- Coach and guide team leaders on field-based personnel management, with the support of Human Resources colleagues, ensuring that labour law is adhered to, and NP Human Resources policies are known and implemented.
- Ensure sufficient level of staffing, identifying the need for new recruitment in a timely fashion.
- Participate in recruitment panels for South-based recruiting.
- Support Team Leaders to ensure that all field team staff (programme and programme support) receive timely performance reviews in close coordination with HR department.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Master’s degree in project management, conflict resolution, conflict transformation, peace studies, international relations, political science, negotiation, mediation, human security or related area of study.
- 4-6 years work experience in civilian protection, violence prevention, social cohesion, peacebuilding.
- Minimum 1 year experience as a Team Leader or similar position with Nonviolent Peaceforce
- Demonstrated management experience in working in complex security environment.
- Demonstrated experience working with state authorities and negotiation
- Demonstrated ability to live, work and solve problems independently and effectively in remote, highly challenging locations
- Demonstrated ability to analyse conflict, security and political contexts
- Identify with NP values and UCP principles

**SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES:**

***Independent Judgment/Analytical:***

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data
- Ability to manage information with discretion
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies

***Interpersonal:***

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work in a multi-cultural environment
- Solutions focused, creative problem solver
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, various community leaders, military, police and non state actors
- Genuine commitment and interest in living and working at the community level
- Flexibility and adaptability

***Language:***

- Ability to interact confidently in English with colleagues and external contacts, to write documents and reports, and to present effectively relevant information
- Working Ukrainian language skills are an added benefit

***Information Technology:***

- Good skills in Microsoft Office applications. Hardware IT skills a definite asset

**Other Specialized Requirements**

- Ukraine is a complex security environment where conditions change rapidly – experience in insecure environments is essential to success in this position

**Working Conditions:**

- This field position may include challenging living conditions, limited access to amenities, and potentially unstable security situations.
- You must be prepared to live in basic or non-traditional accommodation, which may include shared housing, camps, or field-based settings
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols.

**SPECIAL NOTICE**

Nonviolent Peaceforce is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

Nonviolent Peaceforce acknowledges the duty of care to safeguard and promote the welfare of employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, communities we work with, and other stakeholders and is committed to ensuring safeguarding practice reflects statutory responsibilities and government guidance and complies with best practices in the Humanitarian and Development sector. NP expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We prioritise ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. NP also participates in the [Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/). In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**NO FEE**

**We never ask for payment as part of our selection process, and we always contact candidates via our corporate accounts and platforms. If you are approached for payment, this is likely to be fraudulent. Please check whether the role you are interested in is posted** [**here** ](https://nonviolentpeaceforce.org/work-with-us/)**on our website.**

title: Electoral Inclusion and Accessibility Consultant
body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- Organization: UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/185
- Position Title: Electoral Inclusion and Accessibility Consultant
- Duty Station: work from home, with occasional meetings with UNDP
- Duration: 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- Vacancy Date of Issue: 30 September 2026
- Vacancy Closure Date: 07 October 2026
- National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k4qiQaXRNZG8iikxpxj80h4IFCVt95LK/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k4qiQaXRNZG8iikxpxj80h4IFCVt95LK/view)

**BACKGROUND**

UNDP Lebanese Electoral Assistance and Parliament Support Project (LEAPS) has the main objective to achieve an enhanced efficiency, transparency, and inclusiveness of the electoral process in Lebanon towards the upcoming parliamentary elections through enhanced and efficient electoral processes, improved legislation, and inclusive public participation, addressing the challenges hampering the democratic consolidation in Lebanon.

Through a multi-component approach, the project has the intended outcomes of providing technical assistance and support in the following key electoral areas:

1. Enhanced efficiency, transparency and inclusiveness of the electoral management and administration through improved institutional capacity and legislative reforms;
2. Strengthened institutional capacity of the SCE to perform its mandate and attributions in a sustainable and independent manner;
3. Effectiveness and transparency of the EDR mechanism enhanced through technical assistance to the Constitutional Council,
4. Inclusiveness and participation of vulnerable and marginalized groups in the electoral processes enhanced and
5. Strengthened institutional capacity of the parliament to function, debate and adopt key reform legislation.

war operational context into a focused set of feasible institutional and policy measures ahead of the upcoming parliamentary elections.

The initiative responds to accessibility and electoral-continuity challenges arising from damaged public infrastructure, displacement and continued instability, particularly in the South. It focuses on four priority reforms:

1. Accessible Mega Centres;
2. Reactivation of the Administrative Committee established under Decree 2214/2009;
3. Pre-registration and choice of polling location, including displaced voters; and
4. Inclusive voting and candidacy procedures.

The consultancy will provide specialized technical expertise on electoral inclusion, accessibility and disability-inclusive electoral processes. It will support PWD NGOs in translating available evidence, legal and institutional

provisions, and identified barriers into practical policy proposals and an implementation roadmap for the upcoming parliamentary elections.

The assignment will support:

- Consolidation and analysis of evidence from the 2025 electoral monitoring exercise, previous UNDP-supported activities, relevant legal and institutional provisions, and available information on post-war polling-centre accessibility and availability.
- Development of four concise, evidence-based policy briefs covering the four priority reforms.
- Development or technical validation of minimum accessibility criteria for Mega Centres, covering physical access, transport and parking, internal circulation, voting facilities, signage, accessible information, communication support, emergency procedures and reasonable accommodation.
- Targeted institutional consultations with relevant electoral and government stakeholders, including documentation of responsibilities, feasible options, required data, agreements and outstanding issues.
- Technical input to accessible public communication products and the four short accessible videos, ensuring consistency with the proposed reforms.
- Technical support to the preparation of Commitment Day and the resulting commitment matrix, ensuring commitments are specific, attributable and suitable for follow-up.

**2. SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Governance and Rule of Law CTA and in close coordination with the LEAPS team, the consultant shall:

**A. Evidence Review and Analysis**

- Consolidate evidence from PWD’s 2025 electoral monitoring, previous UNDP-supported work, relevant legal and institutional provisions, and available information on damaged or inaccessible polling centres.
- Identify key accessibility barriers affecting voters and candidates with disabilities, distinguishing verified evidence from information requiring validation.
- Assess the implications of displacement, damaged infrastructure and access constraints, particularly in the South.
- Identify relevant institutional mandates, coordination needs and priority actions.

**B. Policy Development and Accessibility Framework**

- Provide technical input to four concise policy briefs, outlining the issue, evidence, proposed solution, responsible institution and required action.
- Develop or validate minimum accessibility standards for Mega Centres, covering access, transport, circulation, voting facilities, signage, interpretation, communication support, emergencies and reasonable accommodation.
- Ensure recommendations are rights-based, practical and operationally feasible.
- Contribute to an implementation roadmap with responsible institutions, actions and indicative timelines.

**C. Institutional Consultation and Coordination**

- Support the preparation and technical facilitation of consultations with the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities and other relevant government and electoral stakeholders.
- Prepare briefing materials and technical inputs for consultations.
- Document agreed actions, responsibilities, required information and outstanding issues.

**D. Accessible Communication and Commitment Day**

- Provide technical input to four accessible videos, ensuring consistency with the policy recommendations.
- Coordinate with the Media and Communications Specialist on accessible and consistent public messaging.
- Support the preparation and delivery of Commitment Day, including presentation of the four reforms and supporting evidence.
- Contribute to a commitment matrix capturing stakeholders, commitments, next steps and indicative timelines.

**E. Quality Assurance and Reporting**

- Review outputs for technical accuracy, clarity, consistency and alignment with project objectives.
- Ensure recommendations clearly identify responsible institutions and required actions.
- Incorporate UNDP feedback and finalize outputs within agreed timelines.

**3. EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 2 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month).

**4. INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

With day-to-day management the designated project manager or institutional focal point.

UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.

Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**5. DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months without exceeding 18 working days per mo

**DUTY STATION**  
The consultant will work from home, with occasional meetings with UNDP.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Sociology, Humanities, International Relations, Development studies, social sciences, or a related field is required.
- Experience: A minimum eight (8) years of relevant experience in work related to Persons with Disabilities (PWDs), PWD-led organizations, civil society, human rights, social inclusion, participation, rights-based programming, or disability-related research and data.
- Language: Fluency in English and Arabic.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

title: Mission France - Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque F/H
body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e : Médiateur.ice Interculturel.le - Basé à Dunkerque.

**CONTEXTE**

La Mission France de MSF porte assistance aux personnes migrantes en situation de grande vulnérabilité sociale, médicale et/ou psychique sur le territoire français et mène des actions de plaidoyer pour faciliter leur accès au droit commun.

Depuis décembre 2017, la Mission France apporte une assistance aux personnes migrantes.

Elle assure la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, juridique et sociale des personnes exclues des soins de santé et plaide en faveur de l'accès aux soins des personnes étrangères vulnérables, notamment les femmes vivant dans les campements du dunkerquois.

La Mission France compte actuellement trois projets :

- En Ile-de-France. Le projet est ouvert depuis décembre 2017. Orienté dès les origines sur la prise en charge médicale, psychologique, sociale et juridique des mineurs non accompagnés en recours (accueil de jour et hébergement), il a connu une évolution importante en se spécialisant sur le public des jeunes filles en recours de reconnaissance de minorité. S’y ajoute une activité de clinique mobile animée par une équipe de bénévoles
- A Calais et sur le Littoral Nord. Ouvert à l’été 2023. Accueil de jour pour mineurs non accompagnés offrant répit et activités ; cliniques mobiles à destination du public général (adultes, familles, mineurs), incluant des activités de santé mentale. Des activités saisonnières viennent compléter les activités avec, du printemps à l’automne, une activité de maraudes littorales à destination des personnes exilées rescapées de naufrage et en hiver une activité de mise à l’abri des personnes les plus vulnérables.
- A Dunkerque. Le projet vise à répondre aux besoins croissants des femmes, jeunes filles et familles exilées vivant dans des conditions extrêmement précaires sur le Littoral Dunkerquois. En partenariat étroit avec le Refugee Women’s Centre, il se concentre sur la prise en charge médicale en santé des femmes (gynécologie, suivi de grossesse, santé sexuelle et reproductive), une prise en charge en santé mentale, un dispositif d’abri d’urgence pour les femmes seules, le renforcement de la détection et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles, ainsi qu’un volet de documentation et plaidoyer sur les violences et l’absence de services essentiels sur le territoire.

Le volet communication et plaidoyer est central sur cette mission qui évolue dans un pays ayant les moyens d’accueillir dignement mais qui néglige volontairement les populations migrantes.

**Mission**

Soutenir la communication et l'interaction entre les bénéficiaires (migrant.es et réfugié.es) et l’équipe pluridisciplinaire, en traitant les conséquences des barrières linguistiques, des différences socioculturelles et de la discrimination, en suivant les protocoles et les procédures de MSF, afin d'améliorer l'accès à des soins de santé de qualité et à d'autres services pertinents et de permettre de mieux comprendre les déterminants socioculturels locaux.

**Responsabilités**

Faciliter la relation entre les patient.e.s et les prestataires de soins impliqués dans les consultations médicales, de soin de santé somatique et mentale ainsi qu’entre les patient.e.s et la prise en charge par l’équipe sociojuridique :

- Fournir un interprétariat de qualité entre l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patientes dans leur langue maternelle, en prenant en compte l’aspect interculturel, la sensibilité et la clarté de la communication entre les parties.  
    Aider l’équipe pluridisciplinaire et les patient.e.s à remédier aux conséquences négatives des différences socioculturelles et identifier et signaler les obstacles qui entravent l'équité et l'égalité dans l'accès aux services.
- Accompagner et suivre les patient.e.s vers les structures d'orientation (établissements de santé et de soins sociaux) si nécessaire.
- Soutenir l'intervention thérapeutique/sociale en partageant avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire les aspects pertinents du contexte culturel du patient, en agissant en tant qu'intermédiaire culturel.le.
- Participer aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.
- En collaboration avec les autres membres de l'équipe du projet, fournir des informations aux patientes sur le fonctionnement du système de soins et des autres services de soutien (abri, nourriture, transport, soutien juridique) fournis par MSF et d'autres acteurs, dans le but de favoriser la responsabilisation et l'autonomie des patientes.

Contribuer à la compréhension du contexte et à la collecte de données sur les questions médicales et sociojuridiques, en accordant une attention particulière aux vulnérabilités, afin de fournir des informations fiables pour la prise de décisions opérationnelles :

- Assurer une traduction linguistique et interculturelle de qualité lors de la collecte de témoignages à des fins de plaidoyer et de communication.
- Apporter un soutien à la mise en oeuvre d'évaluations ou d'enquêtes, le cas échéant.
- Rapporter toutes les informations importantes exprimées par les patientes et les communautés, en garantissant la confidentialité à tout moment.
- Apporter un soutien à l'analyse des médias et à la création de contenus à des fins de communication.

**Responsabilités spécifiques à la mission France**

Sous la responsabilité de la Coordinatrice projet Dunkerque et en collaboration avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire, le.la médiateur.ice interculturel.le :

- Participe à la réflexion et l’adaptation des activités d’aller-vers mises en oeuvre par MSF sur le littoral Nord, ainsi que plus spécifiquement des activités de santé sexuelle et reproductive sur le Dunkerquois.
- Accompagne les différent.es professionnel.les (soignant.es, pyschologue.s, travailleur.seuses sociaux.les) en tant qu’intermédiaire linguistique et interculturel.le pour assurer un interprétariat en direct lors des consultations, des activités externes, des cliniques mobiles, des groupes de discussions, sensibilisation, formations, des maraudes, des activités d’allers vers et autre cas échéant et permet aux collaborateur.ices d’offrir une qualité de soins et/ou de soutien psychosocial à la hauteur des standards de l’association.
- Sensibilise le reste de l’équipe à des codes culturels qui pourraient être une barrière à l’accès aux services.
- Accompagne dans les activités pour l’identifications des besoins exprimés lors des activités.
- Participer à l’éducation à la santé des femmes et à la promotion des services en santé sexuelle et reproductive
- Tester, diffuser et animer des supports et activités de sensibilisation et d'éducation à la santé auprès des communautés.
- Apporte un soutien à l’élaboration d’outils linguistiques et communicationnels en support aux activités à destination des personnes accompagnés, en collaboration avec l’équipe pluridisciplinaire.
- Participer à l’élaboration des plans de sensibilisation et de mobilisation communautaire.
- Contribuer à l’identification des groupes cibles et des canaux de communication appropriés.
- Animer des séances de sensibilisation, causeries éducatives et campagnes communautaires.
- Assurer la promotion des bonnes pratiques de santé au sein des communautés.
- Mesurer le niveau de compréhension et l'adoption des messages clés.
- Documenter les retours, difficultés et bonnes pratiques observées.
- Participe à la formation des équipes partenaires et/ou du personnes accompagnées dans le cadre des activités sur le nord littoral et en particulier sur le Dunkerquois
- Contribue au recueil de témoignages et s’inscrit dans la démarche MSF en termes de communication et de plaidoyer concernant les enjeux humanitaires
- Participe à la collecte et la capitalisation des données individuelles de suivi des situations médico-psycho-sociales des personnes rencontrées.
- Participe aux réunions pluridisciplinaires.•Participe la communication et la coordination adéquate avec les autres organismes et institutions déployés ou consultés.
- Soutient les autres activités des projets de Calais et du Littoral Nord en cas d’absence prolongée de besoins sur le Dunkerquois.

**Profil recherché**

**Education :**

- Enseignement secondaire essentiel, diplôme souhaitable en sciences sociales, en communication sociale ou en enseignement.
- Formation en médiation interculturelle ou en interprétariat est un atout.
- Connaissance de la protection sociale, de la protection de l’enfance, des dispositifs d’accueil et de prise en charge des mineurs non accompagnés souhaitable.
- Connaissance des dynamiques migratoires et de la population affectée souhaitable.

**Expérience :**

- Expérience dans la traduction et / ou la médiation culturelle souhaitée
- Expérience souhaitable auprès de publics en situation de précarité, d’adolescents ou de jeunes majeurs

**Connaissances et compétences :**

- Permis de conduire B fortement souhaité
- Travail en équipe & Coopération
- Flexibilité
- Gestion du stress et capacité à travailler en environnement difficile
- Sens du service
- Compréhension des enjeux liés à a prise en charge de survivantes de violences sexistes et sexuelles et de traite d’êtres humains
- Adhésion aux principes de MSF
- Maitrise de l’outil informatique (Word, Excel, etc.)

**Langues :**

- Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais.
- Connaissance obligatoire d’une des langues suivantes : tigrinya, amharique ou somali.
- La connaissance de l’arabe est un atout : arabe, farsi, kurde-sorani, allemand.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDD de 3 mois à temps plein 39H / semaine. Poste basé à Dunkerque avec possible déplacement sur le nord littoral (Dunkerque). Pas de télétravail.

**Rémunération :**

- **2 767,75€** mensuels brut sur 13 mois.
- 22 jours de RTT par an. Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100% par Médecins Sans Frontières.
- Titres restaurants d’une valeur faciale de 12.00€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF).
- Prise en charge à 50% du titre de transports en commun ou Kms de vélo.

**Poste à pourvoir :** dès que possible

*En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.*

title: Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups
body:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Endline Evaluation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement II Programme and Syria & Lebanon Top Ups**

**Commissioned by | ActionAid - Arab Region**

**Syria and Lebanon | 2022–2026**

**1. Background**

ActionAid Arab Region (AAAR), together with its local partners, has implemented the Strategic Partnership Agreement II funded by DANIDA in partnership with ActionAid Denmark in Syria and Lebanon from 2022 to 2026. The programme has been implemented in highly complex and protracted crisis contexts, requiring continuous adaptation to changing political, economic, humanitarian and protection conditions.

In Lebanon, implementation has been undertaken with SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh, and RDFL, with interventions reaching communities in Tripoli, Jeb Jenine and Ba'albek.

In Syria, implementation was initially concentrated in Northwest Syria, through Violet and Bahar, and subsequently expanded to Latakia and Damascus in response to changing contextual and humanitarian needs.

The programme has also been complemented by two Top-Ups, one in Lebanon and one in Syria, which are included within the scope of this endline evaluation. The evaluation should therefore assess the overall contribution and performance of the core SPAII programme alongside the additional interventions and adaptations introduced through the Top-Ups.

The programme as a whole is expected to have reached approximately:

- **75,000+ people in Syria**, including people benefiting from humanitarian assistance in its various forms, including distributions, protection services and legal services; people participating in trainings; people accessing youth and safe spaces; and people participating in campaigns, collective action and other forms of civic engagement.
- **35,000+ people in Lebanon**, through similar combinations of humanitarian assistance, protection and legal services, trainings, youth and safe spaces, campaigning and collective action.

The programme has been structured around three Strategic Objectives:

**SO1: Rights and access to services**

**Young people, especially marginalised young women, enjoy fundamental rights through improved access to well-resourced programmes and public services in fragile situations.**

**SO2: Sustainable livelihoods and green solutions**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised young women, enjoy improved, sustainable livelihoods through government that is accountable towards building sustainable green solutions.**

**SO3: Resilience, protection and rights**

**Young people from refugee and host communities, especially marginalised women, are resilient to shocks and enjoy their rights to protection in protracted crises.**

The programme's Theory of Change (ToC) provides the overarching logic through which interventions are expected to contribute to improved rights, access to services, livelihoods, resilience, protection, collective action and longer-term systemic change.

Given the duration and complexity of the programme, the endline evaluation provides an opportunity not only to assess the extent to which the programme achieved its intended results, but also to examine how and why change occurred, the contribution of different interventions and partners, the quality of technical capacity and collective action, the programme's policy influence, and the extent to which programming remained relevant and adaptive in protracted crises\*\*.\*\*

**2. Purpose of the Evaluation**

The primary purpose of the endline evaluation is to provide an independent assessment of the performance, contribution and learning of the SPAII programme and its Top-Ups in Syria and Lebanon between 2022 and 2026.

The evaluation will assess the programme against the OECD DAC evaluation criteria of:

1. **Relevance** – Is the intervention doing the right things?
2. **Coherence** – How well does the intervention fit within its wider context and other interventions?
3. **Effectiveness** – Is the intervention achieving its intended objectives and results?
4. **Efficiency** – How well have resources been used to achieve results?
5. **Impact** – What difference has the intervention made?
6. **Sustainability** – Are the benefits, capacities, relationships and changes likely to continue?

In addition, the evaluation will place particular emphasis on the programme’s ability to adapt to changing and protracted crisis contexts, the quality and adequacy of ActionAid/AAAR’s technical leadership, guidance and support, the effectiveness and quality of collective action, the extent and nature of policy influence, and the relationship between programme implementation and the Theory of Change. The evaluation is expected to generate practical, forward-looking evidence and learning to inform future AAAR programming in Syria and Lebanon, the design of regional and country-level programmes, partnership and localisation approaches, adaptive programming in protracted and rapidly changing crises, technical leadership and support to partners, advocacy and policy influencing, youth engagement and collective action, and humanitarian-development-peace programming. Ultimately, the findings will contribute to AAAR’s organisational learning and strategic decision-making, helping to identify what worked well, where the programme could have done better, why particular approaches succeeded or underperformed, and what should be sustained, adapted or strengthened in future programming.

**3. Evaluation Questions**

The following questions should guide the evaluation. The evaluator should refine and prioritise these during the inception phase.

**A. Relevance**

1. To what extent did SPAII respond to the priority needs, rights and aspirations of young people, particularly marginalised young women?
2. To what extent did interventions remain relevant as the contexts in Syria and Lebanon changed between 2022 and 2026?
3. How well did the programme balance immediate humanitarian needs with longer-term rights, resilience, livelihoods and systemic change?
4. Were there important needs or groups that the programme did not adequately address?

**B. Coherence**

1. How well did SPAII complement other interventions implemented by AAAR and partners?
2. To what extent did the programme create meaningful links between humanitarian response, protection, rights, livelihoods, resilience and advocacy?
3. How well did interventions align with local systems, priorities and existing services?

**C. Effectiveness**

1. To what extent did SPAII achieve its intended outputs and outcomes?
2. Which interventions and approaches contributed most significantly to results?
3. Which interventions were less effective, and why?
4. To what extent did the programme achieve meaningful changes beyond activity and output-level results?
5. What factors enabled or constrained effectiveness?
6. Were there significant differences in results across countries, locations, partners, groups or types of intervention?

**D. Theory of Change**

1. To what extent did the programme's Theory of Change accurately explain how change occurred?
2. Which pathways of change were strongest?
3. Were there unexpected pathways or outcomes?
4. What contextual factors influenced the pathways of change?
5. What should be retained, modified or removed from the ToC for future programming?

**E. Efficiency**

1. Were resources appropriately allocated across interventions and locations?
2. To what extent did the programme achieve value for money?
3. Were programme resources sufficiently flexible to respond to changing needs?
4. How did partnership arrangements affect efficiency?
5. Were there significant operational or coordination constraints affecting implementation?

**F. Impact**

1. What meaningful changes can be attributed or plausibly contributed to by SPAII?
2. What difference did the programme make to young people's rights, resilience, protection, livelihoods and participation?
3. What unintended positive or negative effects emerged?
4. To what extent did the programme contribute to changes beyond direct beneficiaries?

**G. Technical leadership and guidance**

1. To what extent did AAAR provide adequate technical leadership and guidance to support the quality and effectiveness of SPAII implementation?
2. How well did AAAR's technical support respond to the specific realities of Syria and Lebanon, including the constraints associated with protracted crisis contexts?
3. Where were technical leadership or guidance gaps identified, and how did these affect implementation or results?
4. What technical guidance, systems or approaches should be retained, strengthened or developed for future programming?

**H. Collective Action and Policy Influence**

1. What was the quality and significance of collective action supported by SPAII?
2. To what extent did young people influence decisions, institutions, policies or public discourse?
3. What evidence exists of policy or systems-level influence?
4. What enabled or constrained meaningful youth participation?
5. Which collective action approaches should be continued or scaled?

**I. Adaptation in Protracted Crises**

1. How effectively did the programme adapt to changing political, economic, humanitarian and social conditions?
2. Which adaptations were most significant? Were adaptations timely and appropriate?
3. What enabled effective adaptation? What constrained adaptation?
4. Did adaptations maintain alignment with the programme's strategic objectives and ToC?
5. What does SPAII demonstrate about how programmes should be designed and managed in protracted crises?

**J. Sustainability**

1. What programme benefits are likely to continue after funding ends?
2. Which capacities, systems, relationships and practices are likely to be sustained?
3. To what extent have local partners been positioned to continue the work?
4. Are collective action and youth engagement mechanisms likely to continue?
5. What institutional or contextual risks threaten sustainability?
6. What should AAAR and partners do to strengthen sustainability?

**4. Evaluation Scope**

The evaluation will cover:

**Lebanon**: Tripoli, Jeb Jenine, Ba'albek

**Syria:** Northwest Syria, Latakia, Damascus

The evaluation should ensure adequate representation of different geographic and contextual settings rather than relying solely on the most accessible locations.

**Time period**

**2022–2026**

**Programme scope**

The evaluation will cover:

- Core SPAII interventions;
- all Top-Ups;
- all three Strategic Objectives including: humanitarian assistance; protection services; legal services; trainings and capacity strengthening; youth and safe spaces; livelihoods-related interventions; campaigns and collective action; advocacy and policy influence; partnership and localisation approaches; programme adaptation and learning.

**Partners**

**Lebanon**: SHIFT, Bassmeh & Zaitouneh RDFL

**Syria**: Violet, Bahar

**5. Evaluation Approach and Methodology**

The evaluation should use a mixed-methods, participatory and theory-based approach.

A purely indicator-based assessment will not be sufficient. The evaluation should combine quantitative evidence with qualitative investigation of contribution, change, adaptation and learning.

The evaluator is expected to propose a detailed methodology during inception. This should include, as appropriate:

**5.1 Document review**

The evaluation will include a review of key programme documentation, including the programme design and Theory of Change, logframes and IPTTs, monitoring and DQA data, partner and monitoring reports, assessments and previous evaluations, learning and advocacy documentation, Top-Up documentation, and relevant contextual and needs assessments.

**5.2 Quantitative analysis**

The evaluation will analyse available monitoring data to assess programme reach, participation, demographic and geographic coverage, achievement against targets, and trends across the implementation period and intervention types.

The evaluator should critically assess **data quality and limitations** and should not treat reported reach as equivalent to meaningful change.

**5.3 Qualitative research**

The evaluation will use qualitative methods to capture the perspectives of programme participants, young people and marginalised young women, communities, partners, volunteers, AAAR staff, technical teams, duty bearers, service providers, civil society and policy stakeholders.

Methods may include key informant interviews, focus group discussions, participatory reflection, outcome harvesting, contribution analysis and selected case studies, as appropriate.

**5.4 Theory of Change assessment**

The evaluator should conduct a dedicated assessment of the SPAII ToC, identifying:

**Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Outcomes → Strategic Objectives → Longer-term change**

while testing the assumptions and contextual conditions between each stage.

The evaluation should identify successful and unsuccessful pathways of change and explain why they occurred.

**5.5 Case studies**

The evaluator will develop a limited number of illustrative case studies highlighting significant examples of individual or community change, collective action, policy influence, technical leadership and guidance, adaptation to crisis, innovative or alternative solutions, and unintended change. Case studies should focus on the pathways and mechanisms of change, demonstrating how and why change occurred rather than simply describing activities or outputs.

**6. Partnership and Localisation**

The evaluation should assess the partnership model as an important determinant of programme performance.

Questions should include:

- Did partners have sufficient ownership and decision-making space?
- Was technical accompaniment appropriate?
- Did AAAR add value beyond financial support?
- How effective was knowledge transfer between AAAR and partners?
- Were roles and responsibilities clear?
- Did partnership arrangements support adaptation?
- How sustainable are capacities developed through the programme?
- What could AAAR do differently to strengthen locally led programming?

The evaluation should particularly examine the balance between partner autonomy and AAAR technical accompaniment, quality assurance and strategic support.

**7. Ethics and Safeguarding**

Given the sensitive nature of programming in Syria and Lebanon, the evaluation must adhere to ActionAid safeguarding requirements and ethical research principles, including informed consent, confidentiality, anonymity, data protection, do-no-harm and conflict-sensitive approaches, gender-sensitive research, and safe participation of young people. Appropriate referral procedures should be in place where sensitive protection concerns arise. The evaluation should minimise risks associated with discussing protection, legal assistance, displacement, conflict and other sensitive experiences. No personally identifiable information should be included in the final report unless explicitly authorised and ethically justified.

**8. Deliverables**

The selected evaluator/team will be expected to produce:

**I. Inception Report**

Including:

refined evaluation questions; evaluation matrix; detailed methodology; sampling strategy; data collection tools; analysis framework; ethical and safeguarding approach; workplan; limitations and mitigation measures.

**II. Data Collection Tools**

Including appropriate tools for:

KIIs; FGDs; participant consultations; partner consultations; policy stakeholder interviews; case studies; and other proposed methods.

**III. Preliminary Findings Presentation**

A presentation of emerging findings to AAAR and relevant partners for validation and reflection.

**IV. Draft Evaluation Report**

Including:

- executive summary;
- programme background;
- methodology;
- limitations;
- findings;
- conclusions;
- lessons learned;
- recommendations;
- annexes;
- and evidence supporting key findings.

**V. Final Evaluation Report**

Maximum recommended length: **40–50 pages excluding annexes**.

**VI. Learning Product**

A concise SPAII Learning Brief synthesising key lessons and practical recommendations, including what worked and what did not, why, what AAAR and partners should continue or do differently, and what should be adapted to strengthen future programming in protracted-crisis contexts.

**VII. Final Learning Workshop**

Facilitation of a participatory learning session with AAAR and relevant partners to validate findings, identify key lessons and priorities, translate findings into actionable recommendations, and discuss implications for future programming.

**9. Sampling**

The evaluator should propose a purposive sampling strategy that ensures representation across:

- Syria and Lebanon;
- geographic locations;
- partners;
- Strategic Objectives;
- intervention types;
- gender;
- age groups;
- marginalised groups;
- refugees and host communities where applicable;
- direct participants and wider stakeholders.

The evaluation should avoid relying exclusively on programme success stories or easily accessible participants.

**10. Key Evaluation Principles**

The evaluation should be:

**Independent** – providing an impartial assessment of programme performance.

**Utilisation-focused** – producing findings that can directly inform future decisions.

**Participatory** – ensuring meaningful engagement of partners and programme participants.

**Theory-based** – testing the programme's Theory of Change rather than simply measuring indicator achievement.

**Contribution-focused** – recognising that change in Syria and Lebanon cannot necessarily be attributed to SPAII alone.

**Context-sensitive** – recognising the complexity of protracted crises.

**Gender-responsive and youth-centred** – examining who benefited, who did not, and how power and inclusion influenced results.

**Learning-oriented** – identifying not only successes and failures but the reasons behind them.

**11. Key Expected Evaluation Outputs**

Ultimately, the evaluation should answer five practical questions for AAAR:

**A. Where did SPAII get it right?**

What approaches, interventions, partnerships and adaptations generated meaningful results?

**B. Where did SPAII have an opportunity to do better?**

What underperformed, and why?

**C. What actually contributed to change?**

Which pathways in the Theory of Change worked, for whom and under what conditions?

**D. What did SPAII learn about programming in protracted crises?**

How can AAAR become more adaptive, locally led and responsive?

**E. What should AAAR do differently next time?**

What should be continued, stopped, adapted, strengthened, scaled or tested differently?

**12. Timeline**

**Activity Timeline**

Inception phase Week 1

Data collection Week 2 to Week 6

Data analysis Week 7

Validation workshop Week 8

Draft final report Week 9

Final report and learning product Week 10

Final workshop Week 11

**13. Budget**

Maximum 16,230 JODs inclusive of 5% tax for Jordanians and 10% for non-Jordanians.

**14. Required Qualifications of the Consultant/Team**

- At least 7–10 years of experience in evaluation of multi-year development programmes
- Proven experience in youth-led programming, gender justice, climate resilience, and/or humanitarian programming
- Strong knowledge of Jordan context, refugee/host-community dynamics
- Demonstrated experience in designing exit strategies or sustainability assessments
- Strong MEL background, including OECD-DAC evaluations is preferrable
- Experience assessing advocacy and policy-influencing results
- Arabic and English fluency
- Experience working with grassroots organizations and youth structures

**15. Management & Coordination**

- The consultant will report to the AAAR PQMEAL Coordinator and SPA II Programme Manager.
- Local partners in Lebanon and Syria will facilitate, youth mobilization, and access to field sites.
- AAAR will provide project documentation, MEL data, and monitoring tools.

**16. Ethical Considerations**

The assessment must follow ActionAid’s safeguarding principles and ethical standards:

- Do-no-harm approach
- Informed consent, confidentiality, secure data handling
- Gender-sensitive and inclusive methodologies
- Special protection for youth under 18 and refugees

title: Oficial MEAL - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
body:
Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, en el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto, DRC está buscando un/a Oficial MEAL altamente calificado/a con sede en Caracas, Venezuela.

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC administra sus operaciones en Venezuela bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela implementa actividades de monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para personas con necesidades específicas (PWSN), sesiones informativas para personas de interés (PoC), prevención de la trata de personas y seguridad alimentaria.

En el marco de la respuesta de emergencia al terremoto ocurrido en el mes de junio 2026, DRC está abriendo una nueva oficina de implementación en Caracas, independiente de la oficina de país, para atender las necesidades de las poblaciones afectadas. Para ello, busca incorporar un/a Oficial MEAL, es requerida una alta eficacia en el monitoreo y evaluación de actividades para medir la calidad de implementación de DRC en el país.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

El objetivo principal del Oficial MEAL (OMEAL) es apoyar en la implementación de la estrategia para monitorear y evaluar la calidad de los proyectos de DRC en Venezuela, incluyendo la acción en el marco de respuesta a la emergencia por los Terremotos, según indicadores internos, indicadores de donantes, y principios de monitoreo y evaluación estándar. Llevará a cabo actividades operativas de seguimiento a los indicadores, reportes en formatos de donante y control de medios de verificación digitales, levantar alertas de subejecución en el monitoreo mensual a la gerencia, mantener bases de datos y IPTTs actualizados mensualmente y de fácil acceso a los miembros del equipo del proyecto y de la oficina nacional. Bajo supervisión técnica del Gerente MEAL, tendrá que articularse con los equipos de terreno, gerentes técnicos de las bases y coordinadores técnicos programáticos de la oficina nacional de Caracas, para implementar las actividades de monitoreo, en el marco de la estrategia de MEAL.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Monitoreo y Evaluación:**

- Apoyar la implementación de la estrategia MEAL para los programas humanitarios de DRC de las bases a nivel nacional, con mayor énfasis en el apoyo para la respuesta a la emergencia por el terremoto.
- Diseño, implementación y seguimiento mensual de la Indicator Performance Tracking Table (IPTT) para mantener los proyectos asignados al día, con información actualizada y verificada.
- Llevar a cabo actividades de recopilación y análisis de datos cuantitativos y cualitativos de los proyectos asignados.
- Validar y resguardar adecuadamente cada medio de verificación de los proyectos asignados de manera digital y/o física, según corresponda.
- Garantizar la adecuada recolección de datos en los estudios realizados por la organización.
- Apoyar el diseño y la puesta a prueba de herramientas de seguimiento que se utilizarán durante las actividades y la asistencia.
- Apoyar en el diseño e implementación de metodologías de evaluación de los programas DRC.
- Levantar alertas mensuales conforme a la planificación de actividades de los proyectos asignados a la gerencia MEAL nacional.
- Seguimiento mensual a socios implementadores para garantizar un flujo de información bidireccional y una implementación limpia y actualizada de los proyectos asignados.
- Conocer los planes de trabajo de los proyectos asignados, para así proponer estudios de mediciones de evaluación, impacto, sostenibilidad, entre otros, necesarios para garantizar la calidad de los programas desarrollados por DRC en Venezuela.
- Alinearse en la revisión mensual nacional del doble conteo de beneficiarios en la BBDD nacional con el resto del equipo MEAL.
- Apoyar la recolección de datos para evaluaciones (línea base, intermedia y final).
- Coordinar logísticamente el desarrollo de aplicación de encuestas post distribución.
- Coordinar logísticamente encuestas, grupos focales, entrevistas en terreno con apoyo del equipo de las bases.
- Validar que los instrumentos se apliquen correctamente.
- Proveer contexto territorial para la interpretación de resultados.
- Visitas a terreno frecuentemente con el equipo para la validación del uso correcto de los verificadores y llenado adecuado de los mismos.

**Reporte y manejo de información**

- Responsable de la limpieza de las bases de datos construidas para para consolidación de datos a nivel nacional.
- Reportar avance en los indicadores de sus proyectos a la gerencia MEAL, Gerencias Bases, equipos de terreno, socios implementadores y a cualquier otro actor requerido mensualmente.
- Presentar informes mensuales a la unidad MEAL nacional sobre los logros y desafíos relacionados con el monitoreo de los proyectos asignados.
- Producir informes de seguimiento periódicos para garantizar que los programas tengan datos precisos y útiles para informar el desarrollo del proyecto.
- Participar en la evaluación interna del programa.
- Control de calidad y supervisión de los datos que se recogen, realizar visitas frecuentes a terreno para supervisar esta calidad. Identificar y abordar los errores en la recogida y/o en la introducción de datos.
- Participación de las reuniones de revisión de PiP, teniendo la información actualizada de los proyectos asignados, es decir, manteniendo el corte cuantitativo mensual limpio (IPTT) y al día en coordinación constante la Gerencia MEAL nacional.
- Diseño de herramientas visuales que permitan dar avance de las actividades desarrolladas de los proyectos asignados.
- Manejo de bases de datos de los proyectos asignados (query) y producción de información consolidada en power bi – Automatización de sistemas de información.

**Rendición de Cuentas (MPQR):**

- Asegurarse de que las actividades cumplan con los principios de rendición de cuentas a comunidades de DRC.
- Asegurar el uso adecuado de los medios de verificación, establecido para cada programa Humanitario del DRC.
- Apoyar la implementación de los mecanismos de retroalimentación y quejas del DRC Venezuela.
- Durante las actividades de seguimiento, garantizar que los beneficiarios sean tratados con respeto, confidencialidad y consentimiento informado.
- Tener dentro de los proyectos asignados el registro de retroalimentaciones recibidas para rendir cuentas a donantes al respecto.
- Visitas permanentes a actividades de terreno para la verificación de uso adecuado de los canales y la transmisión de mensajes claves.
- Apoyo en la sistematización mensual de las papeletas físicas de los buzones de retroalimentaciones que llegue pro valija a la base de datos nacional.

**Conocimiento de Indicadores del(los) Proyecto(s):**

- Revisar con regularidad el Plan MEAL con los indicadores de los proyectos asignados para verificar el cumplimiento metodológico de los mismos.
- Entender las diferencias entre los indicadores de productos y resultados de los proyectos asignados para poder generar herramientas de seguimiento y de recolección de información adecuadas para dar respuesta a dichos indicadores.
- Estar atento a los indicadores de productos generales de los proyectos asignados, que solicitan ser medidos a través de estudios de línea base, salida o en momentos específicos.

**Gestión y articulación:**

- Servir de enlace con los programas y operaciones para asegurar un seguimiento rápido de la retroalimentación y las quejas recibidas.
- Articularse con la unidad de gestión de la información IM, en el manejo de las bases de datos asignadas.
- Consolidar la base de datos y registros seguros y confidenciales de quejas y reclamos del DRC.
- Articularse con equipos de terreno de las bases a nivel nacional.
- Articulares y comunicarse periódicamente con el equipo MEAL – IM de la oficina nacional.
- Mantener comunicación constante con la línea técnica de la gerencia MEAL de la nacional.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Experiencia laboral de mínimo 3 años en actividades relacionadas con MEAL.
- Conocimiento Avanzado del paquete office (Word, Excel, Power Point, Power Bi).
- Conocimiento de herramientas de recolección de información como Monkey survey y KOBO.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprender.
- Habilidades estadísticas avanzadas y de manejo de información.
- Alta ética profesional.
- Conocimientos básicos de aplicación de la inteligencia artificial a procesos de automatización y eficacia en MEAL

**Deseable**

- Experiencia con SQL, metaverse y otro sistema masivo de administración de datos.
- Experiencia laboral en ONGs nacionales o internacionales es una ventaja.
- Habilidades para trabajar equipo.
- Habilidades para crear / mantener buen ambiente de trabajo.
- Buenas habilidades de comunicación.

**Educación:**

Pregrado en Sociología, Economía, Administración, Estadística, Ingeniería industrial, de sistemas o carreras afines.

**Idioma:**

- Conocimiento inglés hablado y escrito.
- Español

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: 6 meses con disponibilidad de extensión según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.
- Contratación nacional.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC.

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Sabado 10 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio:** Octubre 2026

title: Job Counselor
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

Since 2017, IRC Hellas supports vulnerable youth refugee and host communities in Athens to access income generation through employment and self-employment services and skills-building activities, directly and in collaboration with partners. Building on this experience, IRC Hellas, with the support of UNHCR and in partnership with the Municipality of Thessaloniki, is implementing the Youth Empowerment and Self-Reliance project for the third year to promote socio-economic equal access for vulnerable youth in Thessaloniki.

To support with the implementation of the project, IRC Hellas is recruiting a Job Counselor, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of employability activities, including service mapping, stakeholder engagement, job counseling and Job Readiness Trainings.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Organize needs assessment and service mapping activities related to employability and skills development programming for youth;
- Participate in stakeholder engagement activities;
- Support the project implementation by designing, organizing and leading Job Readiness Trainings and information sessions for youth;
- Support the project implementation by providing individual employment support/job counseling for youth;
- Proactively working to identify issues related to clients’ participation and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensuring relevant project data is accurately collected and updated on a weekly and monthly basis.
- Coordinate closely with the team to ensure effective implementation of the provided activities;
- Participate in regular team meetings;
- Ensure regular reporting from the projects is compiled and reports are submitted to the Senior Livelihoods Manager on a weekly/monthly basis;
- Any other task designated by the Project Manager as requested.

**REQUIREMENTS**

BA/BS Degree in social sciences, education, project management, and/or related certification required. Master’s degree or additional certification in Job Counseling is strongly preferred.

- Minimum 2 years’ experience in training, employment support, counseling or project management, primarily in relation to refugee protection. NGO experience preferred.
- Strong interest in supporting refugees and vulnerable populations (experience supporting youth a plus)
- Demonstrated understanding and ability to maintain confidentiality and respect for clients and partners
- Good interpersonal and strong negotiation skills essential with experience in conflict resolution desirable
- Excellent verbal communication skills
- Strong liaison and diplomatic skills
- Punctuality and attention to detail
- Computer skills, in particular Excel
- Fluency in both Greek and English is mandatory

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

**Working hours:** 9:00-17:00

**Travel and other requirements:** Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs in Greece.

**Disclaimer Clause:** This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skills, effort, duties and responsibilities associated with position.

Due to the expected high number of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: €1,631/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Training Officer
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer for Switchboard, a project that provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:/Users/TigestCo/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Olk/Attachments/ooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe/69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdb/www.SwitchboardTA.org).

The Training Officer will be responsible for leading the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives related to newcomer and refugee services. This role includes providing training and technical assistance to service providers to support them in addressing the general resettlement and case management needs of refugees and newcomers. This role requires prior direct service experience working with clients, subject matter experts, and/or partners to develop culturally responsive service plans to address individual and family client needs utilizing a broad range of approaches, including client-centered, strength-focused, and trauma-informed to meet the social, safety and stability of newcomers.

This staff will be responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective resources, and facilitating learning experiences that contribute to improving outcomes for children, adults, and families.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Develop and deliver training related to refugee and newcomer services, to include webinars, self-paced, e-learning courses, online certificate courses, in-person training, etc.
- Provide consultation, guidance, and recommended resources via email and/or virtual meetings to refugee service providers across the U.S., in response to questions and technical assistance requests
- Produce written learning resources including blog posts, information guides and toolkits
- Incorporate feedback from internal and external reviewers
- Lead development of multimedia resources, including e-learning modules, videos, and podcasts, in collaboration with colleagues across teams
- Coordinate a monthly community of practice focused on refugee and newcomer emerging topic needs

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

*Other duties as assigned*

**Experience:**

**Required:**

- Master’s Degree in a relevant field, such as Master of Social Work (MSW) or equivalent experience.
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience providing pre- and post-arrival services to newcomer clients, supporting their access to educational, financial, medical, social, and community resources while promoting self-sufficiency

**Preferred:**

- Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Master of Social Work (MSW), or equivalent experience
- Direct service work experience in refugee and newcomer education services
- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: IT Business Relationship Director, Americas
body:
**Background/IRC Summary**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

The IRC's Technology department is the engine behind the organization’s ambition to reach 40 million clients by 2033. We are transforming how we work to reach more people through technology and enable faster, better decisions, whilst maintaining a reliable operational foundation that drives down the cost of delivery.

**Job Overview**

We are hiring an IT Business Relationship Director to ensure IT service delivery meets the operational needs of program offices across the Americas geography (US and LATAM), translating business needs into IT priorities and IT technical capability into business value. The role sits at the intersection of IT and program operations — building trust with leadership, diagnosing where IT processes break down, and brokering the cross-office knowledge and escalation paths that don't currently exist structurally.

This role will operate as the connective layer between IT and Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI) and Crisis, Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) leadership across the US and LATAM, working alongside the Global IT Solutions team, the Americas IT Service Desk (POD) and RAI Operations staff. They will build a regular engagement cadence with RAI office and CRRD program leadership, develop enough programmatic fluency to judge whether an IT solution will work in the field, own escalations, knowing when an issue needs IT leadership, a vendor, or executive attention. The role embeds proactive communication and cross-office knowledge-sharing into how IT and program operations work together, so that consistency across offices is structural rather than dependent on individual relationships.

The ideal candidate has direct experience in complex, distributed program operations, and brings credibility with program leadership as a result — not just IT service management experience. They are equal parts relationship manager, translator, and escalation owner: able to build trust with operations staff, assess whether a proposed IT solution will hold up in the field, and judge when to resolve something directly versus route it structurally. They have a bias for proactive communication, a high bar for consistency across offices, and a clear instinct for equipping program and office staff with the tools, access, and know-how to handle their own work.

This role reports to the Senior Director, IT Business Relationship Management and partners closely with RAI and CRRD leadership through an agreed engagement model. The role will also work closely with the Global IT Solutions Team, including the Service Delivery Center of Excellence, Helpdesk team, Enterprise Applications and Infrastructure.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Relationship Management and Engagement**

- Serve as the senior IT partner to RAI office and CRRD program leadership, providing strategic guidance and thought partnership on IT service delivery performance, planned initiatives, and emerging risks across the US and LATAM
- Maintain a regular engagement cadence with RAI operations directors and senior CRRD leadership, ensuring IT priorities are aligned with program needs and that leadership has visibility of service delivery against commitments
- Act as the accountable IT point of contact for escalations from office and program leadership — owning the response, not just the routing
- Build sufficient familiarity with the programmatic context of each cluster to advise credibly on whether IT solutions will work in practice, and to represent office needs accurately to HQ IT
- Own cross-office knowledge brokering — surfacing what's working in one office to others, and serving as the connective point for "what are other offices doing on this?" questions that currently have no structural answer
- Act as the strategic focal point for IT initiative rollouts across RAI offices and CRRD programs in the Americas – shaping appropriate timing, delivery and relaying infrastructure, application, and programmatic IT needs from offices to HQ IT teams and vice versa.
- Support IT budget planning for the Americas region and ensure asset documentation, audit readiness, and regulatory compliance obligations are maintained

**Escalation, Risk Management and Service Performance**

- Own escalation pathways for issues that fall between the helpdesk and engineering teams, knowing when to involve specific IT leads, vendors, or procurement and following through to resolution
- Monitor service delivery performance and key performance indicators across the Americas region, identifying patterns and recurring issues that should trigger problem management review; escalate trending patterns as they emerge for either immediate action, system enhancement, or larger risk management
- Partner with the Global Service Desk Manager on T1/T2 technician performance, ensuring ticket priority logic and SLA adherence

**Job Requirements:**

**Knowledge & Experience**

- 6-8 years in a relationship management, business partnering, or program/operations role bridging technical and non-technical stakeholders — direct experience with humanitarian, nonprofit, or similarly complex distributed-operations environments strongly preferred
- Working knowledge of the IT service and technology lifecycle, from planning and delivery through operations and continuous improvement, sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams and evaluate whether a proposed solution is fit for purpose
- Familiarity with IT best-practice frameworks and delivery models (e.g., ITIL, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent project delivery methodologies) and how they apply to service management and technology rollouts; ITIL Foundation certification preferred, not required
- Demonstrated experience translating operational needs into technical priorities and representing technical capability back to non-technical leadership
- Experience defining and tracking performance metrics (KPIs, SLAs, or equivalent) and running a recurring review cadence with stakeholders

**Personal Attributes**

- Spanish language proficiency
