body:
**Keeping the Story Alive: Strategic Citizen Journalism in Sudan**

## **Project Background**

Sudan’s information ecosystem faces severe challenges amidst ongoing conflict. Professional journalists and citizen reporters operating inside Sudan document critical field realities under extreme pressure, insecurity, and personal risk. Exposure to conflict, displacement, and traumatic events creates a significant psychological burden and complex mental health challenges for frontline reporters.

**Role Objective**

The Psychosocial Support Expert provides mental health and group therapy expertise, designing, facilitating, and delivering virtual group psychosocial support sessions for program participants to process stress and trauma, build coping mechanisms, prevent burnout, and foster peer solidarity in a safe and confidential environment.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Session Design & Preparation:** Tailor group therapy methodologies to the realities of journalists in active conflict zones. Develop sensitive, culturally appropriate, and trauma-informed session outlines focusing on trauma handling, stress management, burnout prevention, and self-care strategies.
- **Facilitation & Group Therapy Delivery:** Facilitate up to 50 virtual group support sessions across designated participant cohorts via secure, encrypted digital tools (e.g., Signal, Zoom, WhatsApp), addressing acute fear, secondary trauma, emotional exhaustion, and operational isolation.
- **Confidentiality, Safeguarding & Risk Mitigation:** Enforce strict participant confidentiality and anonymity protocols. Establish clear referral pathways for individual cases requiring advanced clinical care or specialized psychiatric intervention beyond the scope of group therapy.
- **Reporting & Monitoring:** Provide brief, anonymized quarterly progress summaries and structural feedback to project management (MiCT and Ayin Network), documenting overarching mental health trends and operational observations without revealing identifying details.

## **Key Deliverables**

1. Inception Plan & Session Framework detailing session methodologies, confidentiality protocols, and tailored topic breakdown.
2. Delivery of up to 50 scheduled virtual group therapy and psychosocial support sessions across cohort cycles.
3. Anonymized quarterly progress reports outlining completed sessions, general emotional themes, participant engagement levels, and risk mitigation steps.

## **Qualifications & Requirements**

- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) in Clinical Psychology, Psychotherapy, Trauma Counseling, Social Work, or a related mental health discipline.
- Minimum 5 years of professional clinical experience in providing trauma-informed therapy or crisis counseling.
- Demonstrated experience supporting journalists, human rights defenders, or individuals operating in high-risk conflict settings (prior context experience in Sudan or the MENA region highly preferred).
- Native or professional Arabic fluency (spoken and written) for session facilitation, along with professional working proficiency in English for project reporting and coordination.

Technical competence in digital security practices, safe online facilitation, and managing remote group dynamics in low-bandwidth environments.

title: Senior Health Technical Lead/Specialist
body:
**BACKGROUND**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGOs), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities, helping people survive, reclaim control of their futures, and strengthen their communities.

The IRC was present in Sudan from 1981 to 2009. In November 2019, the IRC re-registered in Sudan and, with the wider IRC-led Consortium (CARE International, Catholic Relief Services, Medical Teams International, Relief International, and local partners), currently delivers integrated health and nutrition services across 11 states, supporting 640 health facilities and service delivery points nationwide and reaching over four million beneficiaries in 2025.

Since the outbreak of war in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the country has spiraled into relentless violence, institutional collapse, and mass displacement, and is facing one of the most complex and devastating humanitarian crises in the world today. More than 30 million people now require humanitarian assistance, and around 25 million people face acute food insecurity, including 770,000 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

The project is expected to run for the duration of the World Bank-financed award (exact start date and duration to be confirmed on award).

**Senior Health Technical Lead Scope of Work**

The IRC is seeking a Senior Health Technical Lead for an upcoming World Bank-funded health project in Sudan. The project is intended to restore access to a basic package of health and nutrition services and preserve the main elements of essential public health functions in Sudan.

The project is expected to run from February 2027 for 3 years.

The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical leadership and quality assurance across SHARE II's health and nutrition service delivery and health system strengthening activities including primary health care and hospital services, nutrition programming (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive, maternal and newborn health, disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness, health information systems (DHIS2/EWARS/HMIS), and facility-level WASH and infection prevention and control. They will ensure service delivery is technically sound, aligned with national health strategies and World Bank requirements. SHARE II will sustain and maintain SHARE I’s existing footprint in delivering a basic package of health services to 420 PHCs and 10 hospitals and also expand access to essential health services in prioritized high-need localities. The project will be delivered nationwide across multiple states including RSF and SAF controlled areas and many areas with severe to catastrophic health needs.

The postholder will lead facility readiness assessments and IPC protocols; oversees nutrition programming and evidence generation; supports health workforce strengthening, referral pathways, and differentiated delivery models; and provides technical guidance on DHIS2/HMIS, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness and emergency response, climate-resilient facility and WASH improvements, laboratory and blood systems, digital health, and supply chain/pharmaceutical management, coordinating closely with Consortium partners.

The Senior Health Technical Lead represents the IRC-led consortium in relevant technical coordination mechanisms (Health, Nutrition and WASH Clusters, Strategic Advisory Group, technical working groups), liaising with WHO, UNICEF, and Federal/State Ministries of Health, and reinforcing government-led systems. They ensure technical activities comply with World Bank Operational Policy 7.30, the Procurement Regulations, and the Environmental and Social Framework, including SEA/SH prevention and response; supports the Third-Party Monitoring mechanism, IRC's Community Feedback Mechanisms and the project's Grievance Redress Mechanism; and supports continuity of SRH and GBV services across the Consortium.

The Senior Health Technical Lead supports the phased, consultative handover of SHARE I sites into SHARE II, ensuring continuity of services, staffing, incentives, commodities and data systems during transition, and contributes to sustainability and responsible exit planning, including integration into MoH plans. The Senior Health Technical Lead provides technical inputs to project reporting, including results framework/indicator tracking for submission to the Project Director and the World Bank, and supports capacity building of MoH and local partner staff consistent with IRC's Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS).

**Requirements**

- Medical degree (MD/MBBS) or an advanced degree (Master's) in public health, health systems management, or a related field.
- Minimum 10-15 years' progressive experience in health systems strengthening and/or PHC and hospital service delivery programming, including significant experience in Sudan or comparable fragile, conflict-affected, or access-constrained settings.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in health and nutrition and relevant technical areas including PHC/hospital service delivery, nutrition (CMAM/IYCF), communicable and non-communicable disease management, reproductive/maternal/newborn health, GBV/SRH, mental health, disease surveillance and outbreak response and health information system.
- Prior experience on large health and nutrition projects financed by the World Bank or other major institutional donors; familiarity with health cluster coordination.
- Experience working with, or through, Ministry of Health structures and health-sector coordination mechanisms (Health Cluster, WHO, UNICEF).
- Strong data analysis, facility assessment (HeRAMS), and technical report writing skills, and demonstrated experience supporting multi-partner consortium coordination.
- Fluency in English required; Arabic strongly preferred, given the requirement for field-facing engagement with MoH/SMoH counterparts and communities.
- Ability to travel to field locations across Sudan, including hard-to-reach and access-constrained areas, and to operate effectively under insecure or volatile conditions, in line with IRC and UNDSS security protocols.

Please note that this position will be contingent on the outcome of the bid.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Youth Education Specialist (YESOL)
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Background/IRC Summary:**  
The International Rescue Committee responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well-being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. Since 1999, the IRC has developed partnerships with New York City public schools, community-based organizations and local colleges and universities to support the positive development of refugee youth and their communities in New York City. The Education and Learning Program provides year-round programming working directly with refugee youth, their parents and families, and their schools.

**Job Overview/Summary:**  
The Youth Education Specialist (YESOL) will work closely with the Youth Programs Supervisor to support high-quality programming for refugee and immigrant youth in New York City. The specialist will be working on a team that works on youth programs including, but not limited to, Youth Tutoring, online Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes, Leaders in Training (LIT), a college access and career readiness program for high school juniors and seniors, World Explorers, a cultural awareness program, and sports programming. During the annual Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA), the Youth Education Specialist will provide logistical support to teaching staff, coordinate instructional coaching, coordinate classroom assessment materials, and collect, enter, and analyze assessment data, ensuring the overall day-to-day classroom needs of the Academy are met. The specialist will also support with instruction and field trips during Mini-NYSA programs, which occur during school breaks in the middle of the school year.

**Major Responsibilities:**

This position will lead Youth English for Speakers of Other Languages (YESOL) classes:

**Curriculum Preparation**

- Create and improve YESOL curriculum to meet the needs of current student population, including academic English and test preparation
- Prepare slideshows for each class
- Update syllabi for each group as semester progresses

**Intake and Assessment**

- Manage new referral and contact information, outreach to potential families and students
- Administer baseline, midline and endline English assessments, coordinate intake process
- Collaborate with parents and teachers to identify specific student needs

**Teach YESOL Classes**

- 2-3 groups of Middle School: Beginner and Intermediate
- 2 groups of High School: Beginner and Intermediate
- Additional groups based on student need and program capacity

**YESOL Program Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Track class attendance and document daily individual and class case notes
- Gather qualitative data of program impact through student surveys and staff observations
- Synthesize and present data for annual reports

**Intern Management**

- Recruit and hire Youth ESOL interns
- Delegate weekly tasks and review submitted projects and tasks
- Provide opportunities for leadership and professional development

**Saturday Parent ESOL Classes**

- Take lead on managing ESOL classes for parents of youth programs students

**Mini Newcomer Youth Spring Academy (Mini NYSA) and Newcomer Youth Summer Academy (NYSA) Support** — direct responsibility for the academic program

- Support NYSA program planning, including staff and volunteer recruitment, hiring, and training
- Plan and instruct lessons on ESOL and other topics to groups of up to 25 students
- Participate in all Meet & Greets, staff trainings, program meetings, and staff development activities thereafter
- Assist the Dean of Instruction in the implementation and analysis of various student assessment initiatives, including but not limited to content area assessments, progress reports, and report cards
- Monitor submission of, enter, and analyze student assessment data
- Assist in the timely production and dissemination of necessary assessments and resources for all teaching staff
- Assist in the coordination and set up of caregiver-teacher conferences
- Assist in the coordination and implementation of school-wide Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS)
- Lead the coordination and implementation of all staff-appreciation events and initiatives
- Lead groups of students for off-site field trips
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position reports to: Youth Programs Supervisor
- Position directly supervises: Interns
- Other internal and/or external contacts: Other youth program staff

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in education or relevant field; Master's degree candidate in education preferred
- Must be available for Saturdays to run programming
- Strong command of Microsoft Suite, G Suite, Canva, and other digital platforms required
- Classroom teaching experience preferred (both in-person and online, especially TESOL experience)
- Experience with data collection and analysis
- Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail
- Strong written and oral communication skills
- Cultural competence and cross-cultural or overseas experience required
- Experience working with immigrant populations, highly desirable
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team
- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapting programming to shifting client needs and relevant government policy changes
- Fluency in written and spoken English required. Second language proficiency in relevant language highly desirable (including Spanish, French, Dari, Farsi, Pashto, Arabic, Tibetan, Russian, Haitian Creole, Ukrainian, Mandarin, etc.)
- Flexibility to work on Saturdays and evenings based on program requirements

**Working Environment:**

- All applicants must be based in or willing to work from our New York City office
- The IRC NYC RAI office currently operates on a hybrid schedule (3 days in office, 2 remote)
- During Mini-NYSA and NYSA, the specialist is expected to work in-person Monday–Friday at a centrally located public school in New York City
- During school-year programming, the specialist will be expected to work Tuesday–Saturday
- Online ESOL classes during the school year take place after school hours; specialists should expect school-year hours of 11am–7pm, Tuesday–Friday
- Saturdays are in-person at the IRC office from 9am–5pm

***This position is expected to end on August 31, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $27.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Head of Programme Nigeria Abuja
body:
**About the Context**

Nigeria continues to face a complex and protracted humanitarian crisis driven by armed conflict, insecurity, climate-related shocks, displacement, and economic challenges.

The Northeast remains the epicenter of the crisis, where years of conflict have displaced millions of people and disrupted access to basic services, livelihoods, and protection. In addition, increasing levels of violence and displacement in the Northwest and North Central regions, alongside recurrent flooding and food insecurity, have further exacerbated protection and humanitarian needs across the country.

The 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan estimates that 5.9 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been operating in Nigeria since 2015, delivering humanitarian assistance and durable solutions to conflict-affected and displaced populations. NRC works across multiple core competencies, including Education, Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Shelter, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and Protection from Violence. Through direct implementation and partnerships, NRC supports displaced persons, returnees, and vulnerable host communities to meet their immediate needs, strengthen resilience, and pursue long-term recovery and self-reliance.

NRC is committed to principled humanitarian action, safeguarding, accountability to affected populations, and ensuring that assistance reaches those most in need**.**

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The purpose of the Head of Programme position is to develop and ensure implementation of holistic high-quality programmes. In this role you will provide strategic leadership and oversight for the Country Office’s programme portfolio, ensuring that projects and interventions are effectively designed, implemented, monitored, and aligned with the organization's mission, strategy, and donor requirements. Additionally, you will be responsible for driving programme quality, impact, accountability, and growth while ensuring efficient use of resources and compliance with organizational policies.

**What you will do**

1. In collaboration with the Programme Unit, lead the development of the Country Office fundraising strategy. This includes the mapping of donor policy and priorities and their alignment with NRC’s programmatic and advocacy goals.
2. Lead the development and implementation of NRC’s partnership strategy in Nigeria, ensuring effective collaboration with national and international partners, strengthening partner capacity, and promoting principled, equitable partnerships in line with NRC’s partnership framework.
3. Responsible for contributing to the development and implementation of country strategy.
4. Responsible for the coherence and quality of core competency programmatic input to all relevant processes and documents;
5. Responsible for strengthening our collaboration with other actors through building and strengthening networks, cooperation and implementing partnerships
6. Responsible for ensuring sound and timely grants management through NRC’s Project Cycle Management (PCM) framework and in line with donor requirements and best practice.
7. Responsible for ensuring consistency and promoting synergy between programme and support units
8. Acting Country Director (CD) when delegated

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- A bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (programme management, business or a social science related). An advanced academic qualification will be an added advantage.
- Minimum 5 years’ experience from a senior management position in a humanitarian/ recovery context with responsibility for programme and/or project management
- Experience in NRC Core Competency programming is an asset.
- Experience of working on, coordinating or leading consortia or other forms of partnership implementation.
- Experience in MEAL systems and approaches, and accountability mechanisms and frameworks.
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities.
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile.
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal and excellent drafting skills.

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the Central and West Africa context and crisis;
- Experience with start-up, scale-up projects, emergency and early recovery contexts.
- Experience of mainstreaming evidence-based approaches to programme quality throughout the project cycle.
- Experience of working in integrated programmes.
- Knowledge of donor landscape, priorities and conditions.
- Effective team building, cross-cultural communication and conflict resolution skills;
- Experience in the design and delivery of team capacity strengthening, including remote coaching, mentoring and training.

**2.Behavioural competencies**

- Strategic thinking.
- Initiating action and change.
- Empowering and building trust.
- Managing resources to optimize results.
- Handling insecure environments.
- Deliver Results
- Act with Integrity

Find more details [Job Description\_Head of Programme Nigeria.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAppsIWsn8pSrnsXD_8p7suATL_WSPKx1hUS6Wuia5fbLw?e=1wfFUD)

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Abuja, Nigeria
- Contract: 24 months
- Salary&benefits: grade 11 on NRC’s salary scale (The contract can be national/resident and/or international/mobile depending on final selected profile)
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

title: (Senior) Research Officer for Nigeria, Based in Dakar
Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) Team Member
body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) Team Member**.

## **About the job**

The EORE Team Member position is created within the Libya programme team under the Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP) sector for the BRIDGE project (Building Resilience through Integrated Services for Displaced and Host Communities in Greater Libya, Enhancing Well-being), funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS). The project is being implemented in partnership with INTERSOS (Lead agency) and WeWorld.

The team member is responsible for performing all assigned HMA tasks within his/her respective team, based on his/her training and qualifications and as assigned by the Project Manager (PM) and EORE Team Lead. This includes risk education and awareness-raising (EORE), victim assistance (VA) and data collection/ survey, support delivery of various training related to VA and EORE, and advocacy, ensuring full support for DRC’s mine action operations in Libya.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Overall responsibilities:**

- Conduct all assigned mine action (MA) activities safely and in accordance with DRC Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Conduct Victim Assistance and EO Risk Education in targeted communities following the operational plan as prepared.
- Maintain high standards of discipline and conduct, working collaboratively with team members, leaders, and managers.
- The EORE Team Member reports primarily to the EORE Team Lead on all matters.

**Specific tasks:**

- Collect data (community information, victims, accidents, and any other information relevant to the project) from the targeted area.
- Support EO victims/ survivors and their families, including the delivery of assistive devices and referrals within DRC and beyond.

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least Minimum 1 year of previous experience in EORE and VA programming.

**Education:**

title: Endline and Final Evaluation Assessment for GAC funded project
body:
Oxfam is a global movement of people who are fighting inequality to end poverty and injustice. Across regions, from the local to the global, we work with people to bring change that lasts.

[**Click Here**](https://oxfam.box.com/s/s73dy36skscd8fr1p89qur4xjno9i6an) to view the post overview

**BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT**

The purpose of this Terms of Reference (ToR) is to outline the scope, responsibilities, and deliverables for a consultant (individual or firm) who will be responsible for conducting an endline assessment and final evaluation for the Global Affairs Canada (GAC)-funded project “Reducing GBV and Inequality through Lifesaving WASH and Protection: An Integrated Response to Crisis-affected Communities in Yemen, Lebanon and Syria” (2024–2026). The project aims to reduce suffering and improve the protection environment for crisis-affected communities, especially women and girls, including GBV survivors and persons with specific needs, through improved, equitable and gender-responsive access to protection and WASH services. The consultant will be expected to conduct a final evaluation and endline assessment of the project to measure its progress toward achieving the desired outcomes, including both originally planned and adaptive interventions introduced in response to emerged challenges. The two products are commissioned as a single combined assignment, delivered as one consolidated report with a distinct Endline Findings section and a distinct Final Evaluation section, so that the same data collection tools, samples and fieldwork can serve both purposes. As detailed below, the consultant's role differs by country: in Lebanon and Syria the consultant leads data collection, analysis and reporting directly; in Yemen, data collection will be carried out by Oxfam's Yemen office team, with the consultant responsible for the analysis and reporting of that data.

**PROJECT BACKGROUND**

The project is funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) over a duration of 24 months. Its Performance Measurement Framework ([Annex 8](https://oxfam.box.com/s/gknwbf42ooyp7ekvdxbp2v7qqv6xepx9)) sets out 53 indicators across the ultimate, intermediate, immediate outcome and output levels, disaggregated across Yemen, Lebanon and Syria.

The project seeks to reduce gender-based violence (GBV) and inequality and improve access to lifesaving assistance for crisis-affected communities in Yemen, Lebanon and Syria, through two integrated components:

- Protection: Strengthening safe, confidential and informed use of lifesaving, gender-responsive protection services, including GBV services, legal assistance, and cash for protection, and building the self-protection capacity of communities and frontline actors.
- WASH: Enhancing equitable use of lifesaving, gender-responsive WASH services — including drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene — while reducing the risk of GBV associated with WASH service delivery.
- Women Leadership in humanitarian action: Including training and support mechanisms provided to enhance local women's leadership in and influence over humanitarian response.

The project is implemented through local partners in each country: in Yemen, the Field Medical Foundation (FMF, WASH activities in Al-Qubaytah, Lahj governorate) and the Coalition of Humanitarian Relief (CHR, WASH and protection activities in Maqbanah, Taiz governorate); in Syria, the Syrian Society for Social Development (SSSD) and the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch and the East's Development Department (GOPA-DERD); and in Lebanon, the Association NABAD for Development (NABAD), KAFA (Enough) Violence & Exploitation, and the Lebanese Center for Human Rights (CLDH).

The results chain below summarizes the results levels the project is working toward:

[Click here ](https://oxfam.box.com/s/ew8z5kfpsox12ssnultdezs8ddxq7cxq)to view the results level

**PURPOSE, OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The purpose of this assignment is to conduct an endline study and a final evaluation of the GAC-funded project “Reducing GBV and Inequality through Lifesaving WASH and Protection: An Integrated Response to Crisis-affected Communities in Yemen, Lebanon and Syria.”

**The final evaluation**

The final evaluation aims to assess the project's overall impact, effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence, and sustainability at the end of its implementation period. The evaluation will examine how the intervention contributed to more systematic, safe and confidential access to protection and GBV services, and to enhanced, equitable and gender-responsive use of WASH services, across Yemen, Lebanon and Syria. It will also analyze the project's adaptability in response to evolving crises and access constraints, and how such adjustments enhanced the relevance, flexibility, and responsiveness of the intervention. The evaluation will apply the OECD-DAC criteria and review achievements against project targets and outcome indicators, identify enabling and limiting factors, explore unintended effects (including protection and safeguarding risks), and assess the quality of stakeholder engagement, GBV survivor-centred programming, and the project's contribution to localization. The evaluation will provide an independent, evidence-based analysis that ensures accountability to GAC and affected communities while generating actionable recommendations for future humanitarian programming.

**The Endline Study:**

The endline study will collect the final values for the project's key indicators, as set out in the Performance Measurement Framework ([Annex 8](https://oxfam.box.com/s/gknwbf42ooyp7ekvdxbp2v7qqv6xepx9)), to assess overall project performance and progress toward intended results. The endline will primarily measure achievement against end of project targets and, where routine monitoring data exists, changes over the life of the project. Beyond indicator tracking, the endline should also explore the project's contribution to intended and unintended outcomes, an area of particular interest to both GAC and Oxfam — drawing on qualitative evidence (KIIs, FGDs, and the outcome harvesting exercise described under Methodology) to complement the quantitative indicator results. The methodology should be applied consistently across Yemen, Lebanon and Syria to allow for aggregation and comparison, while remaining sensitive to the distinct context, access, and security conditions of each country, including the country-differentiated data collection modality described in the Methodology and Roles and Responsibilities sections below.

**The scope of this assignment**

The scope of this assignment covers all three project countries (Yemen, Lebanon and Syria), all outputs and their related outcomes (see results chain and outputs table above), and the full 24-month implementation period. It includes both a quantitative component (household/beneficiary survey against PMF indicators) and a qualitative component (KIIs, FGDs, case studies and an outcome harvesting exercise), covering both the endline indicator results and the analytical final evaluation against the OECD-DAC criteria. It excludes a full financial/value-for-money audit, which falls outside this assignment. The specific evaluation and research questions that define this scope in more detail are set out in the Key Evaluation Questions table below and will be finalized with Oxfam during the inception phase.

**METHODOLOGY**

The key steps to be followed, though not exhaustive, and the detailed modality and work plan will be agreed during the consultation meeting, and include:

**3.1 Endline Study Methodology**

The endline study will focus on measuring changes in key project indicators and will provide quantitative and qualitative evidence of progress toward the achievement of the project’s intended outcomes.

For Syria and Lebanon, the endline methodology should, to the extent possible, maintain consistency with the methodology and data collection tools used during the baseline study. This will allow for more meaningful comparison between baseline and endline findings and support the assessment of changes over the course of the project. Any necessary adaptations to the baseline methodology or tools should be clearly justified and agreed during the inception phase.

**3.2 Final Evaluation Methodology**

The final evaluation will assess the overall performance and strategic value of the project, using a mixed-methods approach grounded in the OECD DAC evaluation criteria: relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability, and coherence. The purpose is to generate evidence-based insights on how well the project achieved its intended objectives, the quality and durability of outcomes, and the lessons learned — especially in the context of protracted crisis, active conflict, and GBV risk.

**Evaluation Design**

The evaluation will triangulate findings from the endline data with additional qualitative and contextual analysis. This will ensure a comprehensive and balanced understanding of project achievements, limitations, and adaptations.

***Key Evaluation Questions***

***Click here to view the key evaluation questions*** [***part one***](https://oxfam.box.com/s/8jcsg43jo4tu1vyfn16t93g4sqnqaw1v) ***and*** [***part two***](https://oxfam.box.com/s/kf4gdrqlexq2fzkrix0nyr97cat7xjbn)

***Data Collection Methods***

- Document Review: Review of all relevant project documents, including the Logic Model, PMF, monitoring data, progress reports, financial records, and conflict/access impact assessments.
- **Household/Beneficiary Survey:** A structured quantitative survey administered to a representative sample of project participants/beneficiaries in each country, to measure progress against the PMF's outcome and output indicators (e.g., access to protection and GBV services, equitable use of WASH services, self-protection capacity). The survey should collect sex, age and disability disaggregated data consistent with the project's M&E approach. The survey will be conducted using a digital data collection platform (SurveyCTO). In Lebanon and Syria, the survey will be built and hosted on Oxfam’s SurveyCTO domain, with access granted to the consultant. Data collection will be administered directly by the consultant’s field teams. In Yemen, the survey will be administered by Oxfam’s Yemen office team. The consultant will be responsible for data cleaning and analysis across all three countries. and quality assurance.
- **Key Informant Interviews (KIIs):** Interviews with Oxfam staff, implementing partners, community leaders, local authorities, and, where feasible and coordinated with Oxfam, a representative of the donor (GAC), to gather insight on implementation, coordination, and crisis response. In Lebanon and Syria, the consultant will conduct KIIs directly (in-person or remotely). In Yemen, KIIs will be conducted by Oxfam's Yemen office team using guides developed jointly with the consultant, with recordings/transcripts shared with the consultant for analysis.
- **Focus Group Discussions (FGDs):** FGDs with representative groups of project participants (e.g., women, youth, persons with disabilities) to capture their experiences and perceptions of project impact. As with KIIs, FGDs in Lebanon and Syria will be led directly by the consultant, while FGDs in Yemen will be facilitated by Oxfam's Yemen office team following consultant-designed guides, with the consultant leading transcription review and analysis. Any engagement with GBV survivors must follow a survivor-centred, do-no-harm approach with safe referral pathways in place.
- **Outcome Harvesting:** A mini outcome harvesting exercise, conducted with Oxfam and partner staff (and, where relevant, community stakeholders) in each country, to identify and verify significant changes including unintended outcomes that the project contributed to, and to substantiate the “how” and “why” behind observed results. This complements the indicator-based endline and strengthens the evidence base for the Impact criterion under the final evaluation.
- **Case Studies**: Where feasible, the consultant may prepare illustrative case studies showcasing successful interventions, adaptation strategies, or stories of impact and resilience, drawing on interviews conducted directly (Lebanon, Syria) or facilitated by Oxfam's Yemen team (Yemen).

***Analysis and Reporting***

Analysis and reporting will be conducted separately for the quantitative and qualitative data collected, then triangulated to produce integrated findings:

- **Quantitative analysis:** Survey data will be cleaned and analyzed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, means, cross-tabulations) to measure achievement against each PMF indicator's end-of-project target, and, where routine monitoring/baseline data exists, to assess change over the life of the project.
- **Qualitative analysis:** KII, FGD, case study and outcome harvesting data will be analyzed thematically, coded against the OECD-DAC criteria and the key evaluation questions, to explain and contextualize the quantitative findings and capture intended and unintended outcomes.

All findings (quantitative and qualitative) should be disaggregated by gender, age, location, disability, and nationality/displacement status (e.g., host community, IDP, refugee, returnee), given the significant presence of displaced and refugee populations across the three countries. The consultant is expected to provide a clear evaluative judgment under each OECD DAC criterion and a synthesis of key learnings and recommendations for future programming. The consultant retains full responsibility for data analysis and reporting across all three countries, including for the Yemen dataset collected by Oxfam's Yemen office team, and is responsible for the overall cross-country synthesis, comparison, and the single consolidated endline and final evaluation report.

***Ethical Standards***

The evaluation must follow ethical principles of do-no-harm, informed consent, data confidentiality, and conflict sensitivity. Given the prevalence of GBV, displacement, and conflict-related trauma across Yemen, Lebanon and Syria, special care must be taken when engaging with affected populations, particularly GBV survivors and other individuals with specific needs. This applies equally to data collection conducted directly by the consultant (Lebanon, Syria) and to data collection conducted by Oxfam's Yemen office team (Yemen), for which the consultant must provide clear ethical guidance, consent protocols, and referral pathway instructions as part of the tools handed over to the Yemen team. The consultant must comply with Oxfam's safeguarding, protection, PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) and ethical data-use standards, and must ensure that tools and protocols follow a survivor-centred approach with safe referral pathways for any disclosure of abuse or protection concerns.

**DELIVERABLES**

This assignment produces the following deliverables, covering both the endline study and the final evaluation as a single combined product:

- Inception report (draft), including the consultant's understanding of the assignment, refined evaluation matrix/questions, detailed sampling approach and unit of analysis, data collection tools (survey, KII/FGD/outcome harvesting guides), and a detailed work plan and risk analysis.
- Final inception report, incorporating Oxfam's feedback, together with finalized data collection tools and, for Yemen, training/orientation materials for Oxfam's Yemen office team.
- Cleaned datasets (quantitative and qualitative) for all three countries, including the Yemen dataset transferred by Oxfam's Yemen team.
- Draft consolidated Endline and Final Evaluation Report, with separate Endline Findings and Final Evaluation sections, including case studies and outcome harvesting results.
- Validation workshop with Oxfam and partners to present and discuss draft findings and recommendations.
- Final consolidated Endline and Final Evaluation Report, incorporating feedback from the validation workshop, comprehensive against the PMF ([Annex 8](https://oxfam.box.com/s/gknwbf42ooyp7ekvdxbp2v7qqv6xepx9)) indicators and the Key Evaluation Questions.
- A short PowerPoint presentation summarizing key findings and recommendations.

The working language for all deliverables is English.

**Planned Timeline**

[**Click Here**](https://oxfam.box.com/s/w57zjgmpjnokfa2sdkwntzruv8hkn20u) to view the planned timeline

**EXPERIENCE OR PROFILE REQUIREMENTS**

Upon the conclusion of an open and competitive bidding process, Oxfam will commission a technically qualified independent consultant (an individual consultant or a consultancy firm/team) with a capable team covering Lebanon and Syria for direct fieldwork, and with strong remote analytical capacity for Yemen. The core team must demonstrate strong expertise in research, baseline and endline assessments, monitoring and evaluation methodologies, statistics, and Protection (including GBV) and WASH sectors. For Lebanon and Syria, the team should include experienced enumerators and data entry personnel, fluent in Arabic and familiar with local dialects, with clear logistical capacity to operate under the current security and access constraints in each country.

Preference will be given to individual consultants or firms with proven experience delivering assignments of similar scale and complexity, and who meet the following qualifications:

- 7–10 years of relevant experience in development research and evaluation
- Proven experience in evaluating Protection (including GBV response) and WASH humanitarian programming.
- Demonstrated capacity in designing and implementing quantitative and qualitative assessments, particularly in the relevant sectors.
- Strong understanding of GBV case management, safeguarding, and PSEA standards, given the sensitivity of protection-related data.
- Strong understanding of research methodologies, data collection processes, and ethical research standards.
- Experience conducting field research with communities in Lebanon and/or Syria, including participatory approaches.
- Strong understanding of gender and protection mainstreaming, and localization approaches.
- Experience working in the MENA region, particularly Yemen, Lebanon and Syria; existing operational presence (registered office, field presence, or established local associates/enumerator network) in Lebanon and/or Syria is a preferred criterion.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, with strong capacity to write high-quality reports in English.
- Ability to propose and manage an efficient, context-appropriate team composition across Lebanon and Syria (direct fieldwork) and Yemen (remote coordination, training and analysis), considering social, cultural, environmental, and security sensitivities.
- Proven ability to work with diverse teams and under pressure to meet tight deadlines while maintaining high-quality deliverables.

title: Call for Syrian Experts: Education in Emergencies, Early Childhood Development & Youth Skills (Syria)

body:
Trust Consultancy and Development is an independent research and third-party monitoring and evaluation (M&E) consultancy based in Gaziantep, Turkey, with two sister-companies, one in Islamabad, Pakistan and one in Erbil, Iraq. Trust provides a range of services and works with partner companies and NGOs in the MENA region and beyond. Our work addresses the growing demand for high-quality research, third-party research, data collection, and data analysis. Our clients include international and national non-governmental organizations and donors, including UNICEF, UNFPA, OCHA, Expertise France, Global Communities, IRC, IMC, DCA, Save the Children, People in Need, World Vision, Norwegian Refugee Council, GIZ, USAID/BHA and ECHO. As a research and M&E company, we offer a unique perspective and can tap into a network of people working on the ground in real time on the issues we research. Currently, we are working in Syria, Turkey, Iraq, Yemen, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.

To learn more about us, please feel free to visit: [https://trustconsultancy.org/](https://trustconsultancy.org/) and [https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/](https://www.linkedin.com/company/trust.inc/)

***About the Internship Position***

body:

Trust Consultancy and Development is an independent research and third-party monitoring and evaluation (M&E) consultancy based in Gaziantep, Turkey, with two sister-companies, one in Islamabad, Pakistan and one in Erbil, Iraq. Our work addresses the growing demand for high-quality research, third-party research, data collection, data analysis and capacity-building services. title: Call for Syrian Experts: Peacebuilding, Social Cohesion & Conflict Analysis (Syria)
International Education Expert
body:
**About STOOS**

STOOS is an international research and consulting firm providing **evaluations, assessments, research, capacity building and project management** services across humanitarian and development settings. We work with NGOs, international organizations and other partners to generate evidence, strengthen programmes and improve outcomes for communities across the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe and beyond.

STOOS invites applications from experienced **international Education Experts** to collaborate on education-related consultancy assignments. **Experts based in any country are welcome to apply.** Assignments will be **primarily remote**, with occasional travel depending on project requirements and agreed availability.

**Role Overview**

The Education Expert will provide technical and strategic support to education assignments, drawing on substantial experience in **managing and implementing education projects internationally**. The role will include contributing to programme design, evaluations, assessments, research and capacity building, working closely with STOOS teams, clients and national partners.

We are particularly interested in experts who combine **practical programme management experience with strong research, evaluation and analytical skills**, and can translate evidence into feasible recommendations for education programming.

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Programme design and technical support:** Contribute to education strategies, theories of change, results frameworks and implementation approaches that improve access, quality, equity and learning outcomes.
- **Project management and implementation:** Provide guidance on work planning, implementation quality, partner coordination, monitoring and adaptive management.
- **Evaluations, assessments and research:** Lead or contribute to education evaluations, needs assessments, feasibility studies and thematic research, including methodology development, sampling and research tool design.
- **Technical analysis:** Assess issues relating to formal and non-formal education, teacher development, inclusive education, education systems and **Education in Emergencies (EiE)**.
- **Data analysis and reporting:** Review programme documentation, analyse qualitative and quantitative findings, and produce clear reports with practical recommendations.
- **Stakeholder engagement:** Facilitate consultations, interviews and workshops with education authorities, donors, implementing partners, teachers, learners and community representatives.
- **Capacity building:** Develop training resources and strengthen the capacities of project teams, local partners and researchers through coaching and technical guidance.
- **Quality assurance and safeguarding:** Ensure deliverables meet agreed standards and integrate **child safeguarding, research ethics, gender equality, disability inclusion and conflict sensitivity**.
- **Proposal development:** Contribute technical inputs to education-related proposals, including approaches, methodologies, workplans and deliverable frameworks.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- A **Master’s degree or higher in Education, International Education, Education Policy, International Development** or a closely related discipline.

**International Professional Experience**

- **At least eight years of professional experience in managing and implementing education projects internationally**, including work across different country contexts.
- Demonstrated responsibility for education programme planning, delivery, team or partner coordination, monitoring and quality assurance.
- Experience working with **international NGOs, UN agencies, donors, government institutions or international consulting organizations**.
- Strong understanding of challenges affecting education access, participation, retention and learning outcomes, particularly for marginalized and crisis-affected populations.
- Demonstrated experience conducting or contributing to **education evaluations, assessments or research**, using qualitative and quantitative methods.
- Experience translating programme evidence into actionable recommendations for implementing organizations, policymakers and development partners.

**Technical and Collaboration Skills**

- Strong analytical skills and the ability to produce **clear, well-structured reports**.
- Ability to develop research tools, review data quality and synthesize findings from multiple sources.
- Proven ability to collaborate with **multicultural teams and national partners**, including through remote working arrangements.
- Strong organizational skills, responsiveness and the ability to deliver high-quality outputs within agreed deadlines.
- Commitment to safeguarding, ethical research and culturally appropriate engagement with children, young people and communities.

**Languages**

- **Fluency in English is mandatory**, including excellent speaking, analytical writing and report-writing skills.
- **Proficiency in additional languages is an asset.**

**Areas of Expertise of Particular Interest**

Applicants may bring expertise in one or more of the following areas:

- **Education in Emergencies** and education in conflict or displacement settings.
- Inclusive education, disability inclusion and gender-responsive programming.
- Teacher professional development, pedagogy and teaching quality.
- Foundational literacy and numeracy, learning assessment and learning recovery.
- Non-formal education, accelerated education and pathways back into formal schooling.
- Education systems strengthening, policy analysis and institutional capacity development.
- Early childhood education and development.
- Integration of child protection, psychosocial support and wellbeing within education programmes.

**Working Arrangements**

Engagements will be **consultancy-based and linked to specific assignments**. Most activities—including document review, methodology development, remote consultations, analysis, reporting and technical coordination—will be undertaken remotely.

The scope, duration, level of effort and fees will be agreed for each assignment. Where travel is required, arrangements will be discussed in advance.

title: Program Officer, Instructional Design & Multimedia
body:
*This position is contingent on receipt of grant funding.*

**Job Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Program Officer for Instructional Design and Multimedia for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org.

This position designs and produces the learning experiences newcomers encounter across Settle In’s platforms. The role combines two areas of practice: instructional design—structuring multilingual, self-paced learning journeys that help newcomers build knowledge over time—and multimedia production—creating videos, graphics, and other assets that support the full range of Settle In content.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Design multilingual, self-paced learning journeys for newcomer audiences, including learning objectives, sequencing, knowledge checks, and reinforcement. Apply instructional design, adult learning principles, plain language standards, and translation-ready structure so that content is usable by newcomers with varying levels of literacy, digital literacy, and prior exposure to U.S. systems.
- In partnership with Switchboard’s Senior Program Officer, Instructional Design, establish instructional design standards for Settle In content and review materials developed by team members, subject matter experts, and contractors against those standards.
- Incorporating Switchboard’s established instructional design standards, recommend and implement improvements to Settle In’s instructional design practice, and update previously developed Settle In learning resources on an established review cycle.
- Create compelling, in-language multimedia content, including short-form video, infographics, motion graphics, and social media assets.
- Manage post-production of all finalized work, including Adobe Premiere project organization, color correction and grading, sound design, motion graphics, music editing, sequencing, export and compression for multiple platforms, and archiving.
- Coordinate with the multilingual Digital Community team on content creation, voiceover, subtitling, and translation review, and advise colleagues on audio and video recording tools and practices.
- Ensure final products are easy to understand, culturally appropriate, linguistically and factually accurate, accessible across web and mobile, and aligned with Settle In standards, newcomer needs, and funder requirements.
- Ensure all learning experiences and multimedia content meet accessibility standards (e.g., captions, alt text, screen-reader compatibility)
- Maintain visual and instructional consistency across Settle In's platforms (website, mobile app, social media)
- Coordinate and incorporate feedback across teams and projects and participate in user testing and other methods for optimization of content.
- Manage production timelines across concurrent projects and coordinate the work of external contractors, including videographers, designers, and translation vendors.
- Use platform data and user insights to set measurable goals for content and assess performance, and contribute to project reports, including monthly activity updates and performance monitoring reports.

*Other duties as assigned.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in instructional design, education, communications, or other relevant field (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum four years of professional experience combining instructional design and multimedia production, including creating multilingual digital content for diverse populations.
- Demonstrated experience designing self-paced learning for adult audiences, including experience with e-learning tools.
- Excellent command of video editing (Adobe Premiere) and graphic design software (Adobe InDesign, Canva), and knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook.
- Working knowledge of plain language principles and digital accessibility standards.
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting).
- Ability to manage complex projects on strict timelines, with excellent written and oral communication skills and strong attention to detail.
- Fluency in at least one of Settle In’s supported languages (Dari, Pashto, Spanish, and Haitian Creole) preferred.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways, and familiarity with ORR-funded programs.
- Ability to translate complex or technical information into clear, visual, and easy-to-understand learning content
- Experience engaging with external subject matter experts, consultants, or production vendors.

**Working Environment:**  This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Case Coordination Caseworker
body:
**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20.97/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Economic Recovery Coordinator
body:
DRC Uganda is currently looking for a highly qualified and motivated individual to join our dynamic team as Economic Recovery Coordinator.

**The overall purpose of the role:**

The Economic Recovery Coordinator will work in close collaboration with the coordination team of DRC Uganda as well as the implementation teams based in the implementation areas providing technical support to DRC and partner teams through capacity building and close coaching/monitoring of programme implementation for all economic recovery activities across the economic recovery core sectors food security, livelihoods, market systems and financial inclusion, and modalities: green graduation approach, regenerative agriculture design; various cash modalities, provide technical support to implementation teams and partners and supervise the development and implementation of the Country Economic Recovery strategy.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**Technical Coordination and Advisory**

- Provide technical advisory to the implementation teams on any stage of programme implementation.
- Lead on creation and roll out of the technical strategy with emphasis on needs of the affected communities, innovation, and environment.
- Support the Head of Programme in creating and reviewing the Country Programme Strategy.
- Provide technical inputs and review proposals, reports, assessments and evaluations in line with the technical strategy.
- Provide technical capacity building to implementation teams and partners through capacity building and close coaching/monitoring of programme implementation for all cash and voucher assistance (CVA) activities and market systems approaches (MSA) across DRC sectors.
- Prepare learning/knowledge products, Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) and guidelines to support overall Economic Recovery (EcRec) sector development and good-practice implementation.
- Initiate and contribute to the systematic assessment of EcRec sector capacity gap analysis, in collaboration with government, partners and other stakeholders, and support the design of initiatives to strengthen capacities systematically.
- Analyze Uganda EcRec sector challenges, trends, programmes and projects, with a focus on EcRec outcomes, using frameworks, analysis and tools available in the sector.
- Support the Programme Managers in the recruitment of suitable qualified and experienced technical field-based staff.
- Support the MEAL Manager in rolling out qualitative and qualitative monitoring and evaluation approaches, aiming to build contextually grounded learning into program activities.

**Representation, Fundraising and Advocacy**

- Proactively lead on DRC’s EcRec representation with relevant Sectors and working groups on country level and area level when necessary.
- Engage with relevant stakeholders including NGOs, donors and government to promote DRC EcRec programme and support sector’s fundraising efforts.
- Actively seek out new viable partnerships for the EcRec sectors.
- Actively seek out appropriate funding opportunities for the sector in line with the sector strategy.
- Produce materials for EcRec programme advocacy to promote awareness, establish partnerships and support fund-raising.
- Interact with global and regional initiatives and partnerships for EcRec Sectors.
- Contribute to and where relevant lead business development initiatives related to EcRec sector.

**Coordination, Representation & Advocacy:**

- Represent DRC at technical coordination forums, as agreed with the Head of Programme
- Maintain close working relationships with technical leads within DRC Uganda, HQ Hub, and HQ to ensure strategy and implementation coherence with overall objectives.
- Take an active role in promoting DRC’s program advocacy messages in relevant coordination forums.
- In addition to the above, the EcRec Coordinator may be asked to carry out other duties requested by the Head of Programme - but always in the scope of this job description.

About you

To be successful in this role, you must have at least 5 years of practical experience in the humanitarian sector and in the thematic areas of food security, livelihoods, agriculture and financial inclusion. Strong experience in implementing livelihoods and financial inclusion interventions, across the entire project cycle. Moreover, we also expect the following.

*Required*

- Master’s degree in political science, international development, economic studies or other related fields
- Practical experience and up-to-date knowledge in:
- Concepts, methodologies and effective ways of supporting Economic Recovery in relation to key DRC activities, including ensuring adherence to centrality of protection principle and a rights-based approach.
- Concepts, evaluation methodologies and design of cash-based assistance programme
- Market assessment and analysis, ability to support the development of market-based programs
- Programme planning and proposal development including budgeting
- Providing direct and remote technical support to operational teams
- Working with local partners, local authorities and other INGOs in s consortium
- Understanding and driving current trends in the area of economic recovery: building self-sufficiency, graduation approach, private and public partnerships, and innovative approaches
- Full professional proficiency in English, including excellent writing skills.
- Experience in facilitating training in the following sectors: graduation approach, agriculture, IGA including development of business plans, entrepreneurship, etc.
- Previous experience working in refugee response in Uganda.
- Ability to communicate technical information in an easy to understand, informative and collaborative manner.
- Good knowledge of the Core Humanitarian Standards or other accountability measures/standards.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence**: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead**: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating**: You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

We offer

- Contract length: 12 months
- Band: NM G1
- Designation of Duty Station: Kampala, frequent travel to programme locations
- Start date: October 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies).

title: Logistics Manager
body:
**What we are looking for**

We’re looking for a **strategic,hands-on logistics leader** who thrives in **complex humanitarian environments** and knows how to turn supply-chain challenges into practical solutions. You’ll bring **strong experience across procurement, supply chain, fleet, assets, warehousing and compliance**, combined with the **leadership skills** to build capable teams, strengthen systems and drive accountability across multiple locations.

If you’re analytical, collaborative, adaptable and solutions-focused, with a track record of delivering under pressure and the confidence to influence both operational and programme decisions, we would love to hear from you.

**Applicants must be legally eligible to work in either Libya or Tunisia, we are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**

**What you will do**

Oversee procurement and logistics management in line with NRC standards, policies and donor requirements, while supporting programme/project implementation and strengthening logistics capacity across NRC Libya.

Key responsibilities:

- Lead and manage the logistics team, setting clear goals aligned to country strategy and priorities, provide training and support to staff and line managers with logistics responsibilities, while strengthening capacity across country offices.
- Lead market analysis and contribute to programme/project design, budgets, procurement plans, transport costs and donor requirements.
- Manage procurement processes (including project and country procurement plans), direct deliveries and stock, fleet, assets and insurance, with regular review of supplies delivery.
- Strengthen compliance, anti-corruption controls and risk management through spot checks, asset and fuel verification, procurement reviews, audit follow-up and remote-management controls.
- Maintain effective logistics filing, reporting and data systems, including implementation of the Warehouse Management System (WMS), Tender Management System (TMS) and other supply-chain business systems.
- Support emergency preparedness and response, area-level partnerships and other logistics priorities as delegated by management.
- Ensure country logistics systems, procedures and operations comply with the NRC Logistics Handbook, NRC policies and donor requirements.

**What you will bring**

- 3–5 years of senior logistics experience (Coordinator, Advisor or Manager) in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Experience in data collection, analysis and report writing, including market analysis.
- Knowledge of leadership skills and ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
- Strong analytical, systematic, collaborative, innovative and adaptable approach.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.

**Context-Specific Skills & Experience**

- Arabic language skills are an advantage.
- Experience with start-up, exit or similar operations.
- Experience with donor rules and compliance, particularly KfW.
- Suppy-chain business management systems.
- Remote management.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQD3qAofiSnyS4Z3TVsX2pU3AYZMG_qypDdcQe31DEYWuR8?e=iaxOjX) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Tunis, Tunisia or Tripoli Libya
- Contract & Duration: Permanent residential contract, subject to funding
- Travel: Up to 25%
