They will manage project resources, supervise staff, coordinate stakeholders, oversee monitoring and reporting, and ensure effective integration of protection, gender, disability inclusion, safeguarding, and accountability to affected populations throughout project implementation.

The PM will support and motivate 3 Project Coordinators and 3 Project Officers to deliver quality implementation in all WASH activities. The PM will also work closely with the consortium partners, building a collaborative and accountable working relationship.

The PM is overall accountable and responsible for implementation of WASH activities under the OCHA funded humanitarian project in Kiryandongo, Palorinya and Rhino Camp refugee settlements. He/She will oversee implementation of activities in two Outcome areas:

- Improved access to safe, reliable and equitable water supply for vulnerable communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.
- Reduced risk of WASH-related disease outbreaks through emergency sanitation and hygiene support for vulnerable refugee and host-community communities in Palorinya, Rhino Camp and Kiryandongo refugee settlements.

**Your main tasks and responsibilities**

***Project planning and implementation***

- Lead in project planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring of progress in line with donor and ZOA requirements.
- Develop detailed work plans, procurement plans, spending forecasts, and activity schedules.
- Ensure implementation is aligned with project objectives, targets, and timelines.
- Conduct regular meetings and direct day-to-day supervision of the field staff to ensure the project is on track towards meeting the work plan requirements, ensuring targets and deliverables are completed by established deadlines.

***Donor Compliance and Grant Management***

- Ensure compliance with OCHA Humanitarian Financing guidelines, partner agreements, and organisational policies.
- Monitor project deliverables, indicators, and reporting obligations.
- Maintain adequate project documentation and audit-ready records.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- Manage project budgets in collaboration with finance staff.
- Monitor expenditure against approved budgets and spending plans.
- Ensure efficient use of resources and timely budget utilisation.
- Identify and address budget variances and financial risks.

***Technical Oversight of WASH Interventions***

- Provide overall supervision of WASH activities, including water supply systems, sanitation facilities, hygiene promotion, and operation and maintenance mechanisms.
- Ensure interventions comply with Sphere standards, Uganda Refugee Response standards, and government regulations.
- Promote quality, sustainability, and accountability in service delivery.

***Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement***

- Represent the organisation in WASH Sector Working Groups, refugee response coordination meetings, and district-level forums.
- Maintain effective collaboration with UN agencies, local authorities, implementing partners, refugee welfare councils, and host community leaders.
- Foster complementarity and avoid duplication of services.

***Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)***

- Ensure routine monitoring of project indicators and progress against targets.
- Review activity reports, field assessments, and monitoring data.
- Support learning, adaptive management, and evidence-based decision-making.
- Ensure community feedback and complaint mechanisms are functional and responsive.

***Team Leadership and Performance Management***

- Supervise project staff, consultants, and field teams.
- Set performance objectives and provide coaching and technical support.
- Promote teamwork, staff wellbeing, and adherence to organisational values and safeguarding standards.
- Ensure the project team has clear objectives, with weekly and monthly targets, to ensure quality implementation of project outputs and outcomes, with regular face to face meetings (weekly or monthly)
- Ensure that project staff are conversant with their job description, ZOA’s internal regulations, standards, policies and donor regulations;
- Supervises and carries out periodical evaluation of the performance of the staff assigned to the project(s) against established performance objectives in a timely manner
- Ensures capacity building on key project concepts and approaches with support from PQ department and/or other ZOA and partner staff; recommends strategic training opportunities for the team;
- Ensures effective leave management within the project team, in liaison with the field Finance and Administration Associate Manager;

***Finance and procurement***

- Uses ZOA’s ERP system to track and maintain oversight of project expenditure (including partner finances), rregularly monitor projects expenditures (using the BVA) to ensure spending is made in line with the budget approved with the donor
- Ensure timely initiation of procurement requests and follow up on progress
- Provide appropriate code for expenses
- Ensure full utilization of the project approved budget, and timely adjustments and communication with the finance team to ensure good budget management.

**Risk Management and Safeguarding**

- Identify operational, financial, security, environmental, and safeguarding risks.
- Develop and monitor mitigation measures.
- Ensure safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) are integrated into all project activities.

***Reporting and Communication***

- Prepare and submit timely, accurate, and high-quality narrative reports for the donor and internally.
- Document project achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and success stories.
- Provide regular updates on project progress, risks, and corrective actions.

***Mainstreaming Cross-Cutting Themes***

- Ensure gender, age, disability inclusion, conflict sensitivity, environmental sustainability, and protection principles are integrated throughout the project cycle.
- Promote meaningful participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, youth, refugees, and host communities in project planning and implementation.
- Monitor equitable access to WASH services and address barriers to inclusion.

***Accountability***

- Sensitize all stakeholders (participants, service providers, partners, government and other) on feedback and complaint mechanisms implemented by ZOA Uganda;
- Upon receipt of a complaint or feedback, ensure that it is correctly documented following correct reporting procedures;
- Work closely with MEAL team to ensure regular analysis of feedback and complaints registered to inform the program of changes in operational trends and context to help in improving the intervention and adaptive management.

**Your profile**

Identity

- The candidate is expected to fully support the vision, mission and Christian values 0f ZOA (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

***Knowledge & Experience:***

- University degree in Hydraulic Engineering, Water Resource Engineering, environmental or public health or other related fields.
- At least 5 years successful project cycle management experience in a similar position; - Experience managing large programmes for INGOs is an added advantage;
- Experience managing large projects funded by institutional donors is an added advantage;
- Having led a project in partnership with a local NGO is an added advantage;
- Excellent spoken and written command of English;
- Language skills in relevant local languages of the duty station is an added advantage.
- Experience of working with People with Disabilities is a plus
- Experience working in the refugee settlement context is advantageous

***Skills:***

- Participative leadership with clear command of overall operations;
- Sensitive towards HRM and organizational issues;.
- Good communication, writing and facilitation skills;
- Innovative, creative and enthusiastic;
- Good computer skills: Ms Excel and Ms Word;
- Self-motivator, able to work with limited supervision;
- Able to ride a motorbike in field conditions, holding a valid driving license.

***Attitude/behaviour:***

- High level of networking capacities, with interpersonal, organizational and intercultural sensitivity
- Commitment to inclusion for People with Disabilities
- Able to plan and coordinate and work in an organized manner
- High level of integrity
- Motivated to work independently / self-managing
- Be a self-starter
- Commitment to ZOA’s mission, vision and values (see [https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity](https://www.zoa-international.com/corporate-identity))

## **About Right To Play:**

For more than 25 years, Right To Play has been protecting, educating, and empowering millions of children each year to rise above adversity through the power of play.

We offer programs in 10 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and North America, reaching millions of children each year in some of the most difficult places on earth, helping them to connect, learn and thrive. We do this by harnessing play, one of the most fundamental forces in a child's life, to equip children with the critical skills they need to dismantle barriers and embrace opportunities, in learning and in life.

This work is supported by our two global offices in Toronto, Canada and London, UK; and seven National Offices in North America and Europe.

Right To Play in Ethiopia is working with government, civil society organizations, communities, teachers and parents to increase access to quality education, enhance primary school children's learning and social emotional skills, promote children's access to inclusive, high quality, play-based Early Childhood Care and Education, provide play-based psychosocial support to improve the holistic well-being of children and young people and address the challenges that children face in host, internally displaced and refugee communities. Learn more about our programs in Ethiopia from [**our website**](https://righttoplay.com/en/countries/ethiopia/).

## **Benefits Highlights:**

- Connect and collaborate with a global team who are passionate about protecting, educating and empowering children and youth using the power of play!
- Culture premised on our **Culture Code (accept everyone, make things happen, display courage, demonstrate care, and be playful)**
- Paid leave (20 days annual leave and 3 personal days per year)
- Competitive benefits such as medical insurance for employee and eligible family members, life insurance for employee, transportation allowance, and communications allowance
- 10% temporary allowance for Ethiopia employees from October to December 2026 and the next salary review is in January 2027
- Learning opportunities and 5 learning and development (L&D) days per year
- Flexible work arrangements
- More information on what we offer is available on [**our website**](https://righttoplay.com/en/landing/why-join-us/).

## **Job Description:**

**Job Title:** Country Director (CD)

**Grade:** 11

**Reports to:** Vice President, Transformation and Impact

**Location:** Ethiopia

**Direct Reports:** Program Manager, Education Specialist, Finance Manager, People and Culture Specialist, MEL Specialist, Logistics Officer

**Department:** Global Program Unit

### **1.Purpose:**

Provides overall strategic and programmatic leadership including business development, fundraising, compliance and risk, financial and people management to ensure the success and growth of the country programme.

### **2.Accountability & Responsibilities:**

#### **Governance and representation (20%)**

- **Identifies and manages organisational risk**, including legal and governance matters, and acts as RTP’s legal representative in country.
- **Represents RTP at country level**, engaging government, donors, UN agencies, and NGO coordination platforms to build influence, credibility, and strategic partnerships.

#### **Fundraising and Communication (20%)**

- **Leads country-level fundraising and resource mobilisation**, driving proposal development, donor engagement, and diversified funding partnerships.
- **Leads in-country media and external engagement**, strengthening RTP’s profile and ensuring alignment with organisational values and objectives.

#### **Strategy development and implementation (15%)**

- **Sets and leads the strategic direction of the country programme**, ensuring alignment with RTP strategy, national priorities, and legal and regulatory requirements.

#### **Programmatic oversight, learning and innovation (15%)**

- **Oversees the country programme portfolio**, ensuring high-quality delivery, measurable impact for children and young people, and timely reporting to donors, government, and HQ.
- **Promotes collaboration and learning**, advising partners on play-based and sport-for-development approaches and embedding evidence-informed practice.
- **Champions innovation and continuous improvement**, driving excellence in programming and efficiency across internal systems and processes.

#### **Operational management (15%)**

- **Provides strategic oversight of finance and administration**, including budgeting, expenditure control, audits, grant compliance, and strong internal controls.
- **Holds overall accountability for safeguarding, safety, and security**, ensuring compliance with RTP policies and national legislation.

#### **Staff and workplace management (15%)**

- **Ensures effective people management**, including recruitment, performance management, learning and development, payroll, and the promotion of a safe and inclusive culture.
- **Leads, mentors, and develops a diverse country team**, fostering staff wellbeing, inclusion, and high performance.
- **Promote Safeguarding, foster a safe, respectful, and accountable work environment** by modelling appropriate conduct and addressing any behaviour that undermines a healthy workplace.

#### **Perform other duties as assigned**

### **3.Scope (geographical and/or functional), Impact and Autonomy:**

Oversees all aspects of the country office, providing guidance and support to the team, while serving on the Global Leadership Team to ensure quality program delivery, adherence to budgets, and contributing to global initiatives that enhance organizational systems and processes.

### **4.Leadership and Staff Management:**

Leads and develops the Country Management Team through coaching, mentoring, and capability-building while championing a safe, inclusive, and high-performing culture. Oversees People & Culture processes to ensure compliance, best practices, and effective performance management, upholding strong DEIA standards, staff safety, and well-being. Demonstrates integrity and resilience, proactively addressing and mitigating legal risks, including seeking legal advice when necessary.

### **5.Information Requirement for Decision-Making:**

Makes decisions based on a combination of internal and external information, often requiring an analytic approach to draw conclusions from incomplete information or non-conclusive information.

### **6.Innovation and Improvements**

Drives innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, impactful programs and more efficient internal systems and ways of working.

### **7. Relationships & Communications: Internal / External:**

Builds and sustains strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government officials, UN agencies, academia, media, NGOs, and local partners, while promoting RTP’s identity and relevance to the needs of vulnerable populations, in alignment with the localization strategy. Leads strategic donor, HQ visits, workshops, represents RTP in high-level meetings, conferences, and media to strengthen its profile.

### **8. Expertise (Certifications / Education, Professional Experience):**

- Extensive experience in leadership roles within a large or medium international development organization, including: strategic planning, leadership and people management, project management and planning, monitoring and evaluation and financial and risk management.
- Master’s degree in business administration, social sciences, development studies or related discipline.
- Experience working in or managing programmes in stable and fragile contexts.
- Proven success with mobilizing new sources of program funding.
- Understanding of laws, regulations and cultural dynamics local and international.
- Fluency in spoken and written Amharic and English Significant experience with a child-focused organization is desirable.

### **9.Core Competences:**

- **Collaboration:** Highly collaborative with strong interpersonal skills; excels at working in with a multicultural team and builds rapport and trust to develop strong external partnerships.
- **Growth Mindset:** Demonstrates commitment to own professional development and encourages their team to develop their potential, creates a learning culture through effective coaching and mentorship.
- **Communication:** Communicates complex operational, technical & strategic issues clearly & credibly to diverse audiences, leveraging strong networks to secure donor funding & influence stakeholders.
- **Resilience:** Strong organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure: multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, solving problems creatively and embracing challenges with resilience.
- **Professionalism:** Models professionalism and RTP’s values, promoting a safe, inclusive workplace and positive impact for children and youth.
- **Management and Interpersonal Skills**: Lead and mentor country team with influence, fostering trust, high performance, and shared ownership of outcome.

### **10.Additional Information:**

Expected to travel regularly domestically and occasionally internationally and work outside regular hours.

title: Global Supply Chain Localisation Advisor
body:
Every year, humanitarian organisations rely on supply chains to deliver life-saving assistance to people affected by conflict, displacement, disasters and crises around the world. Strengthening the role of local actors within these supply chains — and how international and local actors plan, coordinate and deliver together — is a key part of building more sustainable and locally led humanitarian responses

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, is looking for a highly qualified and experienced supply chain professional to help drive this agenda at a global level. In this role, you will contribute to shaping how humanitarian organisations work with local actors and communities, helping ensure that critical humanitarian assistance can be delivered more effectively, efficiently and sustainably where it is needed most

**About the job**

DRC is committed to advancing supply chain localisation as a key strategic objective, working together with the Humanitarian Leadership Group on Supply Chain (HLGSC), a cross-sector initiative bringing together humanitarian organisations, donors and partners to strengthen end-to-end supply chains across the system.

As Global Supply Chain Localisation Advisor, you will provide strategic and technical leadership for the localisation workstream on behalf of DRC, acting as DRC's lead technical representative within HLGSC and working closely with UNICEF and other partners to shape, develop and strengthen the sector's approach to supply chain localisation. You will report to the Director of Supply Chain.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

- Provide technical leadership for the localisation workstream, helping shape the humanitarian sector's approach to supply chain localisation and supporting the delivery of agreed workstream objectives.
- Co-lead the development, testing and refinement of the Supply Chain Maturity Model, assessment methodology and associated guidance in collaboration with UNICEF and other workstream partners.
- Translate concepts, operational experience and stakeholder inputs into practical frameworks, guidance and tools that support localisation objectives across the sector.
- Act as DRC's lead technical representative within HLGSC, bringing DRC's operational experience, NGO perspectives, lessons learned and technical expertise to sector-wide discussions.
- Ensure alignment between the localisation workstream and DRC's wider localisation and supply chain priorities, including partner tiering approaches and partner supply chain management initiatives.
- Work collaboratively with UNICEF, co-lead organisations and technical experts to shape technical direction, build consensus and strengthen workstream outputs.
- Co-lead the technical content and preparation of expert group and technical working group engagements, including consultation materials, draft outputs and decision points for review.
- Provide technical guidance and thought leadership to stakeholders engaged in the workstream, ensuring existing initiatives, evidence and lessons learned are leveraged and duplication of effort is avoided.
- Review, validate and synthesise inputs from expert consultations, technical working groups, bilateral exchanges and testing activities, translating findings into strengthened methodologies, frameworks and recommendations.
- Support the preparation of outputs, recommendations and technical products for governance review, decision-making and endorsement.
- Lead the documentation of lessons learned, evidence gaps, limitations and considerations for the future stewardship, maintenance and evolution of the Supply Chain Maturity Model

To be successful in this role we expect you to bring substantial supply chain experience across HQ and country-office settings, strong technical credibility on maturity and capacity assessments, and the ability to lead and influence across organisations without formal line authority. Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- 7-10 years of experience working in HQ and Country Offices, especially in supply chain and related support functions.
- Supply Chain master's degree or equivalent academic qualification.
- Demonstrated ability to lead technical content development, working within a collaborative co-lead model and influencing, convening and synthesising across organisations without formal line authority.
- Strong track record of representing an organisation in external, multi-stakeholder technical forums.
- Fluency in English is required.

**Desirable**

- Experience working with local partners.
- Experience related to maturity assessments and capacity assessments of partners or markets.
- Familiarity with localisation initiatives (e.g. Grand Bargain / IASC localisation commitments).
- Working knowledge of French.

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC's five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

  
**We offer**

**Contract length:** 12 months, in line with the current implementation period of the HLGSC localisation workstream action — any extension subject is to continued funding and workstream priorities.

**Work location:** Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station. The role requires travel as needed, estimated at once every 3 months.

**Start date:** 1st November 2026

The position is temporary, based on project employment linked to the current 12-month HLGSC localisation workstream action and its funding.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

  
**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Gaurav Verma at **Gaurav.verma@drc.ngo** . We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

**Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.**

title: ICLA Project Manager South Central Syria
body:
**Background**

As the Syrian crisis has entered its 14th year, a record-level 16.7 million people, over 71% of the population, needs humanitarian assistance. Almost half are children. The former government's change in December 2024 sparked hope for the country’s future and for those in need of aid. However, ongoing conflict, economic collapse and record-high humanitarian needs persist throughout the country, coinciding with unprecedented cuts to humanitarian aid globally at a time when aid resources for Syria were already stretched thin.

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been a leading humanitarian actor in the response to the Syria crisis, in Syria and across the region, since 2012. Against a backdrop of conflict, socioeconomic and environmental deterioration, climate change and natural disasters, we provide emergency, transitional, early recovery and resilience programmes to people in need. We lead advocacy to promote unimpeded and sustained access to assistance for people across Syria and we call for increased humanitarian funding, resilience and early recovery support to alleviate the hardships of the Syrian people.

**What we are looking for**

NRC Syria looking for an ICLA Project Manager to join the **South-Central Area Office**. The role holder will be responsible for responsible for managing the overall NRC ICLA project portfolio and staffing in South and Central Syria. They will also contribute to the broader country-level programme development in collaboration with the ICLA Specialist. Additionally, they will contribute to the broader country level programme development in collaboration with the ICLA Specialist.

\*\***\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***

**What you will do**

**The role will have some of the following main specific responsibilities:**

- Lead strategic planning for the ICLA programme in South and Central Syria, including legal needs assessments, gap analyses, and prioritisation.
- Review referral mechanisms for ICLA interventions in South and Central Syria and propose improvements aligned with area office response priorities.
- In close coordination with the ICLA Specialist, review ICLA field team structures and job descriptions to align with strategic objectives, and lead recruitment processes as needed.
- Ensure consistent quality and legal compliance across all ICLA services (legal counselling, information provision, representation, and referrals).
- Ensure accurate and consistent use of ICLA case management and M&E tools and integrate evidence and learning into programme development.
- Oversee legal accuracy of information and advice provided to project participants.
- Support the ICLA specialist in developing and adapting legal tools, case management systems, and training materials.
- Support the ICLA specialist to guide legal research, analysis, and advocacy messaging in line with field evidence and ICLA’s strategic objectives.
- Actively participate in relevant humanitarian coordination forums, including leading the Housing, Land and Property (HLP) Technical Working Group (where relevant).
- Strengthen collaboration with protection actors, legal aid providers, justice sector stakeholders, and local authorities.
- Promote operational synergies between ICLA and other NRC core competencies/programmes.
- Identify staff training needs and coordinate the delivery of legal and soft skills capacity building.
- Participate in and support project start-up, progress review, and closure meetings with relevant inputs and documentation.
- Coordinate new emergency response in Area, and approve existing ones
- Carry out any other task relevant to the position as requested by the Area Programme Manager or ICLA Specialist.

Please download the complete Job Description [here](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAof5x3mHr9Q6lZZ_cV0uFGAd_6avh3Szy0B9zaEF7i0CA?e=Tbejqs) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- **Relevant university degree**, preferably law, human rights or social studies, master’s degree is an added value.
- **Minimum 3 years of experience** in a senior-level legal assistance (or Protection project with significant legal assistance component) project management position in a humanitarian/ recovery context.
- **ICLA (Legal) technical expertise**, including knowledge of **Housing, Land & Property and/or civil documentation issues.**
- Experience working in **complex and volatile contexts.**
- **Fluency in English**, both written and verbal.
- Knowledge of the **displacement context in Syria and the Middle East.**
- Experience with **Legal programming and Legal case management**
- Fluency in **Arabic is a MUST.**

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: **Homs**, Syria.
- \*\*\*\***Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.** \*\*
- Contract: Fixed Term
- Travel: **30-40%** within areas of operation
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC’s national salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- For internal candidates please use your official email address when applying
- Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **mero.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

NRC currently has over 3,000 staff across the Middle East dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya and Palestine. Its humanitarian interventions are based upon its programming expertise in the Core Competencies of Shelter, Education, WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, and Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to vulnerable displaced people that were forced to flee.

 [Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about NRC's operations in Syria [here.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/Syria)

title: Client Voices Promoter
body:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refuges since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

IRC believes that designing our strategies and programs based on clients’ particular needs and preferences is one of the most critical drivers of impact. We also believe that we have a role to play in working with clients so that they can engage as an equal, influential partner both with IRC and in the broader community through advocacy. The Client Voices Promoters will play a key role in supporting client engagement, and feedback initiatives at the local level. Promoters will work to bring together multi-ethnic, multi-racial and multi-sector constituencies to build the power of refugees and immigrants and the organizations that serve them to ensure their sustainability and improve people’s lives.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

- Partner with IRC program staff to execute client satisfaction and feedback initiatives, including surveys and focus group discussions.
- Collaborate with clients to ensure their feedback informs IRC program planning and service improvements.
- Identify and implement preferred client engagement and feedback methods tailored to community needs.
- Act as a liaison between IRC and local refugee communities, representing their concerns and suggestions to office leadership.
- Support client participation in discussions with external partners to amplify their influence on broader community strategies.
- Attend community events and workshops to maintain strong connections with refugee communities and identify areas for program enhancement.
- Organize and facilitate leadership and civic engagement training sessions to empower clients as advocates and community leaders.
- Coordinate community events and focus groups to encourage active client involvement in IRC decision-making processes.
- Ensure alignment with IRC’s client complaints and feedback policies, supporting consistent and ethical practices.
- Maintain accurate records of feedback and engagement initiatives to track progress and inform future strategies.
- Proactively engage with clients and raise their issues to IRC leadership to inform organizational priorities.
- Perform additional tasks as assigned to support IRC’s mission and client-centered programming.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Undergraduate degree preferred, in relevant field of study.
- Minimum 3 years of work experience.
- Demonstrated experience working with refugees, asylees, victims of human trafficking, and/or immigrant populations required.
- Community outreach experience preferred.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and build relationships with colleagues and partners in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment, and the ability to present to a varied public required.
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to juggle multiple tasks, set priorities, effectively manage time, and meet deadlines required.
- Fluency in English, both verbal and written, is required. Fluency in other languages and cultures of the local refugee population including Arabic, Swahili, French and Pashto/Dari is strongly preferred.
- A valid driver’s license, reliable vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area required.

**Working Environment:**

- Combination of working in a standard office environment and work in the community including meetings with community partners.
- Occasional weekend and/or evening work required.

 **Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $20/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Senior Data Engineer (Maternity Cover)
body:
**What we are looking for:**

NRC Norway is looking for an experienced **Senior Data Engineer** for a maternity cover position.

You’ll play a key role in building and optimising the data infrastructure that enables NRC to turn complex data into actionable insights. You will design and maintain scalable data pipelines and ETL processes in Microsoft Fabric across data lakes and data warehouses, ensuring that data remains accessible, reliable, and secure. You will also advise on the use of alternative data products when Microsoft Fabric is not the most suitable solution. Working closely with data product managers, analysts and other stakeholders, you’ll translate business needs into effective data solutions, strengthen data quality and governance, and champion modern engineering practices, automation and innovation.

If you’re passionate about data, technology and meaningful humanitarian impact, we’d like to hear from you.

**What you will do:**

- Ensure that data at NRC is accessible and optimized for use in the organisation.
- Instigate collaboration with program managers and field staff to understand their data needs and ensure that data systems are aligned with operational goals.
- Provide technical leadership, support and guidance to non-technical teams on data processing methods and infrastructure setup.
- Implement best practices for data governance, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and ethical standards.
- Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, guidance and procedures, and a specific responsibility for the functions policies and procedures.
- Build data pipelines in Fabric to integrate internal and external data based on existing internal best

practices. This should reflect the current data needs set by SPK, other operational departments and field operations.

- Contribute to the design and continuous improvement of the Fabric environment, supporting secure data sharing across NRC.
- Contribute to developing the infrastructure, governance, and standards required to make data more discoverable and accessible.
- Build and evaluate systems and data pipelines on Microsoft infrastructure, including Azure and Power Apps, for use cases that fall outside Fabric’s scope, such as archiving solutions, and integrations with other NRC systems.
- Architect the data infrastructure inside and outside of Fabric to ensure it is optimized for performance and can handle the (large-scale) data requirements of the organisation.
- Proactively implement data validation checks, monitoring and error-handling processes to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of data.

Please download a more detailed [**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDKrCT2JlDJS5Zf-TA--9IIAa-KD3fwrJv9-NbZF3szXNU?e=LUSMGu) to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring:**

- Proven experience with IT projects.
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or related subjects, or demonstrable expertise in the field.
- Advanced analytical skills and problem-solving attitude.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, comfortable working with a geographically distributed team, and can easily work with non-technical colleagues
- Capable of operating in an "Agile" environment
- Fluency in written and spoken English. Other languages are an asset.
- Proactive in keeping up to date with industry trends and innovation.
- 5+ years of experience shipping and maintaining code in production.
- Experience working with Microsoft Fabric or other Microsoft reporting tools.
- Experience or deep understanding of data architecture and data modelling.
- Solid knowledge of programming in Python, fundamentals of API design and security, familiarity with basic DevOps is a plus.
- In depth knowledge and comfortable working with relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and nonrelational data (JSON format) including building, optimizing, debugging, and creating queries and safe migration scripts.
- Familiarity in working with enterprise information systems in general, and especially ERP and CRM, are desirable.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC Head Office in Oslo, NRC Representation Offices (excluding Geneva and Washington, DC), approved Employer of Record (EoR) countries, and other countries where NRC operates, provided they are within ±2 hours of Oslo time.
- Contract: Maternity Cover (12 Months).
- Travel: Up to 5%.
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.

title: Country Director, South Sudan
body:
## **Background:**

The humanitarian situation in South Sudan remains one of the most severe and complex crises driven by conflict, economic collapse, climate shocks, disease outbreaks, mass displacement, and shrinking humanitarian funding. An estimated 10 million people will experience critical needs in 2026.

The conflict in neighbouring Sudan continues to drive refugee inflows and returnee movements into South Sudan, placing additional pressure on already overstretched services and humanitarian systems. Over 1 million people have crossed into South Sudan since the Sudan conflict began. Access remains one of the most significant operational challenges due to active conflict, insecurity and bureaucratic impediments making it difficult for aid organizations to reach those in need.

NRC has been present in South Sudan since 2004. Today, it operates in Upper Nile State, Northern Bahr el Ghazal state, Warrap State, Western Bahr el Ghazal Sate, Jonglei State, Unity State and Central Equatoria State

NRC delivers programmes in the areas of Rapid Response to emergencies, Multipurpose Cash Assistance, Legal assistance and Protection, Education, Shelter, Water and hygiene promotion, and places a high importance upon advocacy. NRC co-leads different clusters and working groups (Protection, WASH, Shelter, Land, and Site Coordination Clusters, including HLP and Durable Solutions Working Groups).

**What we are looking for:**

**As Country Director, you will provide overall leadership and responsibility for the country operation. This includes:**

- **provide strategic direction and management to the country programme**
- **drive effective programme delivery**
- **strong external representation, including active engagement in inter-agency coordination**
- **lead resource mobilisation and advocacy efforts**
- **building high-performing teams to deliver accountable, high-impact humanitarian response**

**What will you do:**

The Country Director has overall responsibility for the country operation, providing both strategic direction and operational leadership. S/He leads the Country Management Group (CMG) and is a member of the Regional Management Team, under the leadership of the East and Southern Africa (ESA) Regional Director.

The Country Director provides vision, promotes ideas, gains agreement and acts as a role model. S/he ensures NRC’s continued relevance and position as a principled humanitarian actor in South Sudan.

- Analyse the political and humanitarian context and adapt the NRC programme ensuring relevance to the evolving context in South Sudan
- Prioritise continuous improvement and innovation to ensure the highest quality of humanitarian and protection programming with a focus on timely delivery
- Promote accountability, the highest standards of ethics, including safeguarding and adherence to humanitarian principles
- Drive forward the position and advocacy voice of NRC South Sudan within the changing humanitarian context and ensure that contributions are made to NRC regional and global advocacy efforts. Continue to foster strong relationships with key stakeholders from the government, international community, donors, local actors and the UN.
- In close collaboration with both the Regional Team and NRC CDs from neighbouring countries, jointly set the strategic direction of the regional displacement crisis and ensure close cooperation on developing response modalities.

title: Regional Head of Operational Support
body:
## **Background:**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation dedicated to protecting the rights of displaced and affected people during crises. NRC delivers high-quality programmes to support people forced to flee, helping them rebuild their lives and establish a new future. NRC provides immediate humanitarian assistance, prevents further displacement, and contributes to durable solutions. It operates across both new and protracted crises across 40 countries.

The country programmes in the East and Southern Africa region incorporate Ethiopia, Uganda, South Sudan, Sudan, Somalia, Kenya, and Mozambique. NRC exited from Tanzania in 2026.

NRC has a simplified organisational structure with a leaner Head Office in Oslo and Representation Offices and smaller Regional Teams. Global support structures are established for functions previously managed by the Regional Offices, including Finance, Risk & Compliance, People & Organisation, Media and Communication, PCM & Grants Management. The Regional Team and Country Offices will access support capacity from these Global Resource Pools.

Resource Pools (hereafter pool) gather staff in one common team which is organised and managed (but not necessarily physically located) at Head Office. The purpose of pooling is to improve efficiency, equity, access and flexibility. The teams should ensure predictable access to the same services and deliver them in an efficient way.

In Nairobi Kenya, several members of the different pools are physically located in the regional office, the Regional Head of Operational Support ensures streamlining of hosting arrangements and a conducive working environment for all.

**What we are looking for:**

The Regional Head of Operational Support will ensure an integrated approach to operational management, supporting the quality and timeliness of NRC's response in the region.

The role is responsible for enabling support needs in countries across HR, Risk and Compliance, Humanitarian Access and Safety (HAS), Finance, ICT, Logistics and Administration, ensuring compliance with NRC policies.

The Regional Head of Operational Support plays a crucial role in ensuring that the region is accountable for the performance of country offices, ensuring they meet operational standards and deliver on strategic objectives.

The role ensures a conducive working environment for all teams, including members of different global teams physically located in the regional office in Nairobi.

This role is a member of the Regional Management Team and the Global Support Advisory Group (GSAG) led by the deputy SG/ CFO.

**What you will do:**

- Ensure that support functions within the regional team operate efficiently, fostering a collaborative and effective working environment.
- Hold country offices accountable for progress on their operations by leveraging reports, analyses, and compliance data from NRC’s global resource and pools.
- Support country directors and heads of support, HAS Managers with capacity building and problem-solving related to operational challenges.
- Provide advice and mentorship to country office operational support teams, fostering capacity building and skills development.
- Participate in global discussions on planning and strategy relating to support functions.
- Review of finance, HR and logistics requirements related to regional grants in collaboration with the Global PCM and Grants Management facility.
- Streamline the hosting arrangements for members of global pools physically located in the regional office and ensure a conducive working environment
- The postholder, upon request, can act on behalf of the Regional Director including leading relevant Crisis Management Teams.
