title: Research Officer
Project Coordinator, Childcare Economy, PlayMatters
body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**1. Organization description**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their lives. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities which support them, as well as those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we improve outcomes in the areas of health, safety, economic wellbeing, education and power. Given the disparity faced by women and girls, the IRC seeks to narrow gender inequalities and also ensure social inclusion of all vulnerable groups in broader policies, processes and actions affecting their lives.

The IRC has been working in Ethiopia since 1999 and in Uganda since 1998, supporting refugees, host communities and a range of national and local institutions, including government, community-based organisations, civil society and the private sector. In both countries the IRC implements programming across health, protection and rule of law (PRoL), women's protection and empowerment (WPE), economic recovery and development (ERD), and education, alongside cross-cutting work on systems strengthening and accountability to affected people. The IRC's regional education and early childhood development (ECD) portfolio includes PlayMatters, which promotes learning through play for refugee and host-community children in East Africa.

**2. Job Overview**

PlayMatters 3.0 is the next phase of the IRC-led PlayMatters initiative, funded by the LEGO Foundation. With co-funding from the UBS Optimus Foundation, PlayMatters 3.0 incorporates a new component, **Outcome 4 - Comprehensive Support to the Childcare Economy**. Outcome 4 is led by IRC and will be delivered in **Ethiopia and Uganda** only. It is embedded within the existing PlayMatters programme management structure and leverages the IRC's country operations and partnerships in both countries. As a new component, Outcome 4 is launching an inception phase running until December 2026, with plans for a phased start of implementation activities beginning in January 2027.

Rather than directly operating childcare services, IRC will serve as a systems integrator and ecosystem catalyst, connecting existing and emerging childcare providers to the financing instruments, technical support and policy frameworks they need to sustain and grow their services.IRC in-country staff are envisioned to provide the primary operational presence in both Ethiopia and Uganda, including direct coaching and regular monitoring visits to childcare providers.

Outcome 4 is designed to contribute directly to the higher-order goal of the PlayMatters Theory of Change. Child development outcomes will be anchored in the Nurturing Care Framework (WHO/UNICEF/World Bank, 2018), with a focus on social-emotional learning, safety and security, responsive caregiving, and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) — dimensions particularly relevant to conflict-affected children in Ethiopia and Uganda. Provider economic sustainability will be tracked against a defined set of indicators, including operating cost coverage ratio, cash flow consistency and provider graduation rate, to build the investment case and demonstrate viability beyond the grant period.

To provide day-to-day coordination and oversight of this component, the IRC is seeking a Project Coordinator covering both Ethiopia and Uganda. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for pushing forward all agreed Outcome 4 deliverables with the UBS Optimus Foundation, working in close collaboration with IRC/ PlayMatters country teams, the IRC Ethiopia and IRC Uganda technical coordinators for education and ERD, IRC ECD and ERD technical unit staff, and the technical partners supporting this component

Geographic targeting within Ethiopia and Uganda will be guided by a clear set of selection criteria to be finalised during the inception phase, drawing on the landscape assessment and provider mapping. Where feasible, co-location with PlayMatters 3.0 implementation areas will be prioritised, given the potential for operational synergies and shared community relationships; however, childcare demand, provider density, market viability and government partnership opportunities may point to different or additional geographies. The Project Coordinator will play a central role in this process and should expect a high volume of travel across both countries.

**3. Major Responsibilities:**

**Inception phase and start-up (September – December 2026)**

- Coordinate delivery of the Outcome 4 inception phase workplan across Ethiopia and Uganda, ensuring milestones are met on time and within budget.
- Work with GDI and GSF to finalise the geographic selection criteria, and support delivery of the landscape assessment and childcare provider mapping in both countries.
- Facilitate the process for confirming target geographies, weighing co-location opportunities with PlayMatters 3.0 implementation areas against childcare demand, provider density, market viability and government partnership opportunities.
- Support the recruitment, onboarding and induction of Outcome 4 staff in Ethiopia and Uganda, and establish the operating routines, tools and systems the component will use from January 2027.

**Project planning, delivery and budget management**

- Provide leadership for project planning and scheduling for Outcome 4, from the high-level planning phase to detailed short-term activity scheduling in both countries.
- Track project progress against high-level and detailed plans, troubleshooting and flagging barriers to success with relevant staff and leadership.
- Manage and oversee the Outcome 4 budget, track expenditure across both countries and maintain accurate projections.
- Support country teams to develop, manage and implement key project management tools, such as workplans, spending plans and procurement plans.
- Ensure that project communications are timely, relevant and accurate, including regular status updates to key focal points within PlayMatters, IRC’s Education Technical Unit, and Philanthropy and Partnerships.
- Ensure Outcome 4 activities are integrated with the wider PlayMatters 3.0 outcomes so that synergies and complementarities are realised rather than duplicated.

**Ecosystem coordination and partner management**

- Act as the primary programme focal point for technical partners, ensuring partners are on track with their deliverables, targets and spending.
- Operationalise the systems integrator function: mapping and convening childcare providers, financing partners, technical service providers and government stakeholders, and brokering the connections between them.
- Support engagement with relevant ministries and district and woreda authorities in Ethiopia and Uganda on childcare policy, standards, registration and quality assurance.
- Serve as the main liaison with IRC technical unit focal points for ECD and ERD, ensuring they provide technical insight and support to Outcome 4 activities and objectives.

**Provider support, coaching and monitoring**

- Provide leadership and strategic guidance to the country-level implementation of direct coaching support to childcare providers, drawing on IRC/ PlayMatters in-country staff as the primary operational presence in both countries.
- Plan and undertake regular coordination, advocacy and monitoring visits in Ethiopia and Uganda.
- Support providers to strengthen business practices and to access appropriate financing instruments, working alongside technical and financing partners.
- Identify capacity gaps among providers and coordinate the training and technical support needed to address them.

**Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning**

- Work with the IRC/ PlayMatters MEAL team to operationalise Outcome 4 indicators, including child development outcomes anchored in the Nurturing Care Framework: social-emotional learning, safety and security, responsive caregiving, and MHPSS.
- Oversee routine tracking of provider economic sustainability indicators, including operating cost coverage ratio, cash flow consistency and provider graduation rate.
- Coordinate documentation of evidence and learning to build the investment case for childcare and demonstrate provider viability beyond the grant period.
- Ensure safeguarding, child protection and accountability standards are applied consistently across all Outcome 4 activities, including partner-delivered work.

**Donor and stakeholder relations**

- Coordinate with the International Philanthropy & Partnerships team to ensure that all feedback and requests for information from the UBS Optimus Foundation and LEGO Foundation are timely addressed.
- Contribute to donor reporting, ensuring narrative and financial reporting for Outcome 4 is accurate, evidence-based and submitted on time.
- Represent Outcome 4 in donor-facing conversations, technical working groups and external fora as delegated.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Internal:**

- **Position reports to:** PlayMatters 3.0 Deputy Project Director Technical (based in Kampala, Uganda)
- **Indirect / technical reporting to:** Technical Advisor, Early Childhood Development (based in Nairobi, Kenya)
- **Other internal contacts:** PlayMatters country teams in Ethiopia and Uganda, and related departments within the IRC to ensure smooth workflows
- Managing Deputy Coordinators in Uganda and Ethiopia

**External:** Global Development Incubator (GDI); Global Schools Forum (GSF); childcare providers and provider networks; financing partners and local financial institutions; relevant national ministries and district and woreda authorities in Ethiopia and Uganda; UBS Optimus Foundation, in coordination with IRC Philanthropy & Partnerships; other PlayMatters consortium partners.

**4. Requirements**

The Project Coordinator, Childcare Economy will need to meet the requirements below:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Bachelor's degree in education, early childhood development, international development, economics, business administration or a related field; a master’s degree is an advantage.
- At least 5 years of professional experience in project management, including large-scale, cross-functional, multi-location projects. Experience coordinating delivery across more than one country is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in education and/or early childhood development programming, ideally including work grounded in the Nurturing Care Framework or comparable ECD frameworks.
- Familiarity with the childcare economy, including childcare provider business models, childcare demand and market dynamics, provider financing, and the policy and regulatory environment for childcare provision.
- Understanding of financing instruments relevant to small providers — for example results-based financing, blended finance, grant-to-loan pathways or small business development support — and comfort working with operating costs, cash flow and cost coverage.
- Professional experience responding to complex humanitarian crises and/or post-conflict situations; experience in Ethiopia and/or Uganda is an added advantage.
- Experience managing and supporting partners, including consortium or multi-partner arrangements.
- Experience managing project budgets, tracking expenditure and maintaining accurate projections.
- Experience with training, coaching and staff or partner capacity building.
- Experience representing programmes to donors or clients, ideally including private foundations.
- Willingness and ability to travel frequently between Ethiopia and Uganda and to field locations, estimated at up to 40–50% of working time and higher during the inception phase.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken) is essential, with demonstrated exceptionally strong writing and presentation skills. Working knowledge of Amharic and/or a relevant Ugandan language is an advantage.
- Excellent analytical, presentation, communication and representation skills.
- Strong commitment to the IRC's mission, purpose and values.

**COMPETENCIES**

- Strong cross-cultural communication skills and eager to work as part of a diverse, multi-country team. Sensitive to interpersonal differences and a range of viewpoints.
- Exceptional advance planning and organisational skills. Able to effectively prioritise and follow multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously across two country programmes.
- Analytical, strategic, and able to proactively develop solutions to complex challenges.
- Comfortable with ambiguity. This is a new component in an inception phase: priorities, target geographies and provider partners will be defined as the work progresses.
- Demonstrated creativity and ability to apply innovative thinking and problem-solving skills, particularly where humanitarian programming meets market-based approaches.
- Able to navigate interpersonal and inter-departmental dynamics across country programmes, technical units and external partners to keep focus on goals and products.
- Able to make difficult decisions, as necessary, to ensure that the project stays on track and focused.
- Able to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures, and flexible in adapting to changing requirements.
- High levels of attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
- Reliable and able to work independently while being a strong team player.

**5. Working Environment**

The position will be based in Kampala, Uganda or Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with frequent travel to project locations in both countries. Travel will make up a significant proportion of the role, particularly during the inception phase and the first year of implementation.

IRC security phase classifications vary across operating areas in Ethiopia and Uganda and are reviewed regularly. Current classifications for the relevant locations will be confirmed by the respective country security focal points, and all travel is subject to IRC security clearance procedures. The successful candidate will be expected to comply fully with IRC security policies and procedures in both countries.

The IRC offers a competitive salary and benefits package in line with the applicable salary scale.

**Gender Equality & Equal Opportunity**

We are committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer generous benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce, including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances. We welcome and strongly encourage qualified female professionals to apply.

The IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, colour, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: SOUTH SUDAN - Head of MEAL Department (M/F) - Juba
body:
## ABOUT US

**Desired start date:** ASAP  
**Duration of the mission:** 6 months  
**Location:** Juba

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL (SI) has been operating in South Sudan since 2006, conducting activities in emergency and post emergency context, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas, including refugees/returnees and IDP camp settings.   
Context:  
\- Food insecurity is one of the highest in the world due to recurring shocks (consecutive years of widespread flooding, conflict-based displacement), and an ongoing protracted macro-economic crisis.  
\- The country also faces cholera outbreaks on a yearly basis, has very limited sanitation coverage and safe water access remain a challenge for most of the population.  
\- On top of these chronic situations, South Sudan has been highly impacted by the war that started in Sudan in April 2023. By end of 2025, more than 1,000,000 people had entered South Sudan, the vast majority entering through the Joda/ Wunthow border point in Renk County, Upper Nile State (northern part of South Sudan).   
\- More recently, resurgence of internal tensions have led to heightened conflict and analysts are worried that the peace conditions offered by the Peace Agreement may not hold.  
As a result, 9,3 million are in need of humanitarian assistance as of 2025.   
SI sectors of intervention:   
\- The portfolio includes both WASH & FSL activities. SI's expertise in running emergency WaSH intervention is highly acknowledged by all WaSH actors and donors and has been one of the first responders of the cholera response. Teh FSL component has become very important due to nwe grants that enlarged the portfolio of the mission  
Areas of operation:  
SI has a rapid emergency team based in Juba, who is being deployed following Rapid Needs Assessment in flood, epidemic or conflict induced displacement in the country. The teams will be deployed for up to 2 months per intervention adn the time in the coordination office only for limited time (sectors WASH and Cash). In additiomn, SI has three static offices in Malakal, Renk and Ulang, as well as 2 sub-offices in Fashoda and Baliet, always in Upper Nile.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

To strengthen the quality, accountability, monitoring, evaluation, and learning of humanitarian programmes through robust MEAL systems. The position supports effective monitoring, evidence-based decision-making, accountability to affected populations, data quality, programme adaptation, learning, and compliance with organisational and donor standards.

**The main challenges:**

**Key Issues and Challenges**

- Complex humanitarian access constraints due to conflict, insecurity, intercommunal violence, checkpoints, and bureaucratic impediments, with rapidly changing security conditions.
- High-risk public health environments, including cholera, Ebola, and other outbreaks, requiring strict health, safety, and infection prevention measures.
- Coordination with local authorities to facilitate access, approvals, movement authorisations, and operational continuity.
- Need for technical coordination across sectors, partners, and operational areas.
- Variable team capacity requiring mentoring, coaching, and technical support to ensure quality and compliance.
- Limited communication infrastructure affecting reporting, information management, and operational follow-up.
- Ongoing structuring of the emergency, FSL, and MEAL setup following the recent scale-up, including reinforcement of systems and field capacities.
- High operational pressure requiring flexibility, surge capacity, rapid adaptation, and reprioritisation.
- Logistical constraints including poor road access, flooding, air transport dependency, fuel availability, and emergency supply prepositioning.
- Staff welfare and duty of care concerns linked to deployments in austere and insecure environments.

**Priorities for the first 2–3 months:**

- Strengthen the MEAL department at coordination and field levels, harmonising systems, tools, processes, and reporting with organisational and donor requirements.
- Build MEAL and programme staff capacity through mentoring, training, supervision, and technical support, focusing on data quality, accountability, monitoring, and evidence-based programming.
- Reinforce and operationalise Feedback and Complaint Response Mechanisms (FCRM) and integrate community feedback into programme activities.
- Strengthen information management, data analysis, and reporting to provide timely and actionable information for decision-making.

**Security constraints:**

South Sudan remains a highly volatile humanitarian context marked by conflict, intercommunal violence, displacement, disease outbreaks, climatic shocks, and severe humanitarian needs. Conditions can deteriorate rapidly due to insecurity, political tensions, armed clashes, cattle raiding, flooding, and access constraints, particularly across Upper Nile, Jonglei, Unity, and Greater Equatoria. Bureaucratic impediments, poor infrastructure, and seasonal constraints further restrict access, requiring remote management and air transport.

Juba remains comparatively stable, with access to accommodation, medical services, communications, and facilities supporting staff welfare and coordination. Safety measures include movement tracking, communication protocols, security briefings, contingency planning, and coordination with security actors and local authorities.

Field conditions remain unpredictable. Ulang requires particular attention due to rapidly changing security and access conditions. Malakal and Renk are currently comparatively more stable, while continuous risk monitoring remains essential.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : BA in engineering, Biology, Water Resources Management, Humanitarian/Development/Political Studies, and similar

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years and more

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

**Technical Skills**

1\. Strong knowledge of MEAL systems, methodologies, and tools in humanitarian and emergency response contexts.

2\. Proven experience in designing and implementing monitoring frameworks, indicator tracking systems, and data collection methodologies.

3\. Experience in developing and managing accountability mechanisms, including Feedback and Complaint Response Mechanisms (FCRM).

4\. Strong information management and data visualisation skills, including proficiency in Excel and data management platforms such as Kobo, ODK, Power BI, or similar tools.

**Transversal Skills**

1\. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments.

2\. Strong organisational and planning skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.

3\. Excellent reporting, drafting, and presentation skills.

**Languages**

1\. English mandatory

2\. Arabic is a bonus

## SI WILL OFFER YOU

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Head of MEAL Department lives in a shared guesthouse with the other international staffs (own bathrrom and bedroom but shared kitchen and shared spaces)

- Individual room, with electricity 24/7.
- Internet and Phone network available
- Restaurants and international food are available
- There is an internal curfew at night for international staffs - different zones are set (6-8-10PM). Curfew can be reduced based on security updates
- There is one driver available on evenings for movements out of office hours, 2 drivers during weekends daytime.
- Access to activities is possible for all (and encouraged!).
- In coordination, movements outside of Juba town (besides intervention location) for leisure are not permitted. When deployed in the field the conditions vary and can be challenging.

title: Project Director - PlayMatters
NGO Forum Partnerships & Localization Adviser Syria
body:
**What we are looking for**

NRC Syria is in search of an **NGO Forum** **Partnerships and Localization Adviser** who will provide strategic leadership on localisation and partnership strengthening within the Syria NGO Forum, supporting collective efforts to advance locally led humanitarian action and more equitable, principled, and effective partnerships and improve access to quality funding and decision-making opportunities for Syrian civil society organisations including work related to localisation financing, direct funding, risk sharing, indirect cost recovery, and equitable resource allocation. They will coordinate and facilitate engagement among national and international NGOs, donors, UN agencies, government and other humanitarian stakeholders; lead evidence-based analysis and collective advocacy; and support the development of practical standards, tools, and initiatives that strengthen the leadership, participation, influence, and capacity of Syrian civil society.

Additionally; the position will also serve as a focal point for localisation and partnership issues, ensuring that Forum priorities are informed by evidence, learning, and stakeholder perspectives, and translating emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities into strategic recommendations and collective action.

If you are a dynamic humanitarian leader with extensive experience in localization, partnerships, coordination and stakeholder engagement then this is the role for you!

\*\***\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***

**What you will do**

**The role will have the following specific responsibilities:**

- Localisation Leadership
- Partnership Strengthening
- Advocacy and Representation
- Research and Knowledge Management
- Stakeholder Engagement

Please download the [detailed job description ](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAP7kFVASlFTbNwsl4diuIqARAGPXsmsE_BaLazcqMsVHM?e=MAEVBT)to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- Master's degree in humanitarian affairs, international development, public policy, political science, social sciences, or a related field.
- A first-level university degree combined with significant relevant experience may be considered in lieu of an advanced degree.
- **Minimum 5 years** of progressively responsible experience in **humanitarian action, NGO coordination, localisation, partnerships**, policy, advocacy, or organisational development.
- Demonstrated **experience working with national and international NGOs**.
- Experience facilitating **multi-stakeholder coordination processes and working groups**.
- Proven experience **producing analytical papers, reports, policy briefs, and advocacy products.**
- Experience engaging with donors, UN agencies, and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
- Strong understanding of **localisation debates, partnership practices**, and humanitarian reform processes.
- Experience **managing strategic relationships and influencing diverse stakeholders**.

- Demonstrated **understanding of equitable financing and resource allocation** discussions within the localisation agenda.
- Excellent **facilitation, networking, and consensus-building skills**.
- Strong analytical and strategic thinking abilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to **represent organisations confidently at senior levels.**
- Ability to manage multiple priorities independently.
- Excellent **written and spoken Arabic**.
- **Strong English** languages skills.
- Experience conducting research, surveys, and evidence-generation initiatives.
- **Experience working in Syria or on Syria-related** humanitarian responses.
- Knowledge of the humanitarian coordination ecosystem (preferred).
- Familiarity with **Grand Bargain commitments and international localisation frameworks** (preferred).
- Understanding of **donor compliance frameworks and partnership risk management** (preferred).
- Experience **facilitating dialogue between local actors, INGOs, UN agencies, and donors** (preferred).

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Damascus, Syria.
- \*\*\*\***Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***
- Contract: Fixed Term -renewable based on performance and funding.
- Travel: Approximatley 40%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC’s Syria’s national salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- For internal candidates, please use your official email address when applying.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **mero.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

NRC currently has over 3,000 staff across the Middle East dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya and Palestine. Its humanitarian interventions are based upon its programming expertise in the Core Competencies of Shelter, Education, WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, and Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to vulnerable displaced people that were forced to flee.

 [Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about NRC's operations in Syria [here.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/Syria)

title: WARN Mental Health Advocate
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Mental Health Advocate supports the mental health and resilience of survivors of trafficking through the WARN program, providing one-on-one peer support, referrals, and group-based services. This client-facing role includes one on one support, offering psychoeducation and skill-building workshops, and facilitating MHPSS groups. The Mental Health Advocate also coordinates program logistics, recruit participants, documents services, and supports evaluation through data collection. Additionally, they connect clients to appropriate mental health resources, assist with care coordination, and collaborate with supervisors to provide crisis support as needed.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Client Engagement & Support**

- Provide Psychosocial support including manualized interventions to clients. (Training in interventions will be provided.)
- Develop individualized action plans with clearly defined goals and activities based on assessment findings.
- With support from supervisor, provide health navigation services through referrals for clients requiring higher levels of mental health care to culturally and linguistically appropriate providers.
- Support crisis assessment and intervention for program participants in collaboration with supervisor.
- Represent the WARN Mental Health program at external and internal outreach events.

**Program Facilitation**

- Facilitate psychosocial group programs, ensuring alignment with contract guidelines.
- Facilitate psychoeducation and skill-building group sessions using evidence-based approaches under supervision.
- Recruit and enroll participants for WARN programs.
- Plan and organize logistics for WARN programs, including scheduling, transportation, materials, and space coordination.

**Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Prepare and administer Participant Service Reports with guidance from supervisor.
- Document client interactions and program activities through detailed case notes and data entry.
- Assist in evaluating current services and identifying opportunities for new program offerings.
- Use IRC software to document client information and other program materials.

**Administrative & Team Support**

- Attend and actively participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and relevant IRC trainings and conference calls.
- Collaborate with supervisor and team members to ensure program quality and compliance.
- Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of WARN programming.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** MHPSS Program Manager

**Indirect Reporting:** Clinical Services Supervisor

**Position Supervises:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal***\*\*:\*\* *WARN Team, Family Wellness Team, Resettlement Team, Employment Team, Immigration Team, Youth Program Team, New Roots Team, Health Empowerment Team, Volunteer Coordinator, Finance Team, Operations Team, Development Team.*

***External***\*\*:\*\* *API Chaya, REST, KIND, Northwest Justice Project, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Seattle Police Department, US Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations, Washington Advisory Committee on Trafficking, City of Seattle Human Services Division, Washington State Office for Crime Victim Advocacy, Washington State Task Force Against Trafficking in Persons, and additional partners.*

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant social services field (i.e., social work, human development, psychology) or equivalent professional and/or lived experience with social work, social service provision, psychosocial support, mental health, and community engagement.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant is preferred. However, in lieu of lived experience, experience working with refugees and/or immigrants; cross-cultural or overseas experience accepted.
- Understanding of the systems that intersect with migration and resettlement.
- Understanding of social service system.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Fluency in English and Spanish or other relevant language(s)
- Strong intercultural communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural backgrounds.
- Strong computer, keyboard, email, and general office skills.
- Current driver’s license and valid insurance.

**Working Environment**\*\*\*:\*\*\*

- Standard, professional office environment (flexible remote and in-office)
- Access to a reliable transportation to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area
- Position may involve evening and weekend work and travel

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28-$31/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Country Director - Egypt
body:
**Country Director - Egypt**

**Position Start Date:** October 15, 2026

**Duration:** 24 months

**Location:** Cairo – Egypt

**Status:** family posting

**Terre des hommes does not set closing dates for this position; recruitment is on-going until the position is filled.**

**Tdh:**

The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), with headquarters in Lausanne and an office in Zurich, is the leading Swiss child rights organisation with more than 2000 employees worldwide. We stand together with children to uphold their rights, protect their lives and improve their well-being. We achieve this through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have a positive and sustainable impact.

**Context:**

Since 1983, Terre des hommes in Egypt works in collaboration with recognized national and local partners to provide support and protection to the most vulnerable children, youth, their families, and their communities. Tdh provides a variety of activities in Greater Cairo and across Upper Egypt governorates, with innovative approaches and sustainable solutions to enhance the resilience and wellbeing of the children and youth and help them to build a better future. The interventions are including mental health and psychosocial support, case management, cash assistance, community mobilization, youth empowerment and capacity building to strengthen protection systems and ensure a protective child-friendly environment.

The Children and Youth in Migration sector aims to enhance the wellbeing, resilience, and social inclusion of children and youth affected by migration and displacement by improving their access to essential services, social protection, education, and economic opportunities. It promotes youth empowerment, skills development, and meaningful participation while strengthening the capacities of communities, service providers, and institutions to respond effectively to the needs of mobile and vulnerable populations. Through systems strengthening and livelihood interventions, the programme supports sustainable integration and self-reliance for children, young people, and their families.

The Child Protection sector focuses on reducing the social and economic barriers that increase vulnerability and expose children, youth, families, and communities to rights violations, violence, exploitation, abuse, and harmful social norms. It strengthens prevention and response mechanisms, builds protective environments, and reinforces community and institutional protection systems. By establishing effective protection networks and promoting rights-based and inclusive approaches, the programme aims to enhance safety, dignity, and resilience among individuals and communities affected by or at risk of protection concerns.

The Access to Justice sector strengthens the capacity of justice and social care systems to address the needs of vulnerable children, youth, and families. It supports access to services within social care and justice institutions, restorative justice approaches, and the reintegration of children in conflict with the law. The programme further advances meaningful child participation in juvenile justice processes, promotes gender justice, and facilitates fair and accessible family law proceedings, contributing to stronger legal protections and improved outcomes for those seeking justice.

The health sector is focused on strengthening climate resilience in fragile health systems, ensuring that vulnerable populations maintain access to essential healthcare services despite increasing climate-related shocks and disasters. The initiative aims to retrofit primary healthcare facilities to become climate-resilient, environmentally sustainable, and disaster-ready. By enhancing their capacity to withstand and respond to climate and emergency-related disruptions, these facilities will be able to provide uninterrupted delivery of essential health services during and after crises.

**Responsibilities:**

- He/She ensures the properfunctioning of operations at the national level; as suchhe/she represents the organization in the country.
- He/She directs and supervises all activities connected to the Tdh projects in his/her assignment country in line with Tdh strategic orientations.
- He/She represents Tdh (including legally) and promotes the entirety of its remit in the assignment country.
- He/She demonstrates ethical and exemplary leadership to maintain Tdh good reputation and leads all the Country Office’s collaborators in a shared vision in compliance with Tdh strategic orientations. In collaboration with the programs and expertise, he/she develops the Country Strategy in compliance with the general reference framework.
- He/She develops and guarantees the implementation of the Country Office’s annual plan of action in compliance with the Country Strategy and internal processes (budgetary management, HR and logistics management, quality and accountability)
- He/She guarantees the implementation of an operational risk-management system for the Country Office.
- He/She supervises and supports all staff attached to the Country Office.
- He/She ensures the Country Office’s internal and external communications.
- He/She feels accountable to the beneficiaries, collaborators, and donors.
- He/She makes sure that his/her teams and partners have learned the security policies and the general code of conduct and always comply with them.
- He/She is responsible for the security of the Tdh teams under his/her responsibility and is in charge of the security rules and the contingency plan of the country under his/her responsibility.
- He/She manages and assumes ultimate responsibility for the risks and access aspects of the Country Office.

**More specifically he/she has the following responsibilities:**

Strategy and steering

Representation & external representation

Internal coordination

Security and safety

Human Resources

Finance and logistics

Business development & Reporting

**Profile :**

**Education :** Master’s degree in a relevant field

**Experience, Skills & Competencies** :

Minimum 8 years’ senior experience in an INGO, managing a large team / operation / programme, including previous experience as Country Director

Significant international experience in a humanitarian/refugee/conflict setting

**Languages** : Fluency in English, Arabic an asset

**IT know-how** : Usual MS Office tools

**Salary :**

Expatriate contract under Swiss regulations between CHF 5’000.- and CHF 5’700.- Gross/month according to experience x 13 times, Paid leaves: 25 days annual leaves local accommodation and transportation, Health insurance, accident and medical repatriation insurance, return flight.

**Tdh Global Code of Conduct and Risk Management Policies :**

- Fully complies with Tdh’s Global Code of Conduct and systematically reports any breach to the Code through the whistleblowing procedure: raises awareness within the Foundation on abuse and violence and the rights deriving therefrom, respecting the rights and dignity of children, members of the communities and our own Staff
- Commits to respecting Risk Management Policies including: Safeguarding Policies (Child Safeguarding Policy, Policy on the Protection against Sexual Exploitation and the Directive on Staff Misconduct at the Workplace), Safety and Security Policy and Anti-Fraud/Corruption and Prevention of the Financing of Criminal Activities Policies
- Commits to reducing the risk of abuse and harm by developing a culture of open and informed leadership within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we intervene in.

We offer an exciting and varied work, useful and meaningful, in a team that wants to make a difference for vulnerable children.

title: Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer, POWER Partnership
body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee helps people affected by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and regain control of their future. The Violence Prevention and Response Unit leads IRC's work across women's protection and empowerment, child protection, and protection and rule of law, positioning social work in crises as the connective practice across these areas.

POWER is a multi-country strategic partnership funded by Irish Aid, running from 2025 to 2027 across Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan. Its core logic is holistic gender-based violence prevention and response delivered through strengthened local women-led organizations, including partners such as SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, with a quarter of country budgets channeled directly to local partners under a feminist partnership framework and the PEERS power-sharing principles. The program includes a dedicated advocacy pillar, an emergency response pillar, and a partnership learning pillar, and it works through practices such as women-led safety audits that already constitute community-generated risk analysis feeding into local advocacy and decision-making.

**Job overview**

The Senior Program Quality and Learning Officer coordinates quality and learning across the six POWER country programs. The role works through country WPE and program teams, POWER’s women-led and local partners, and the WPE Global Practice, and coordinates with the Award Management Unit (AMU), which leads the donor relationship with Irish Aid. It is accountable for technical quality assistance against IRC core WPE standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards for the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, and for tracking and reporting delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six countries so that deviation is identified early. The position contributes to the partnership’s advocacy pillar and to the design of the next partnership phase.

**Major responsibilities**

The role holds the technical quality of POWER delivery to IRC's WPE standards, keeps the partnership and the WPE Global Practice in two-way exchange ,rather than a one directional flow of standards downward, and tracks delivery across six countries against scope, timeline and budget so that deviation is flagged early enough for adaptive management

- Provide quality oversight across the six country programs, so that survivor-centered response, case management, women and girls' safe spaces, clinical and MHPSS referral pathways, and social norms work meet IRC WPE technical standards and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Serve as the connective role between the POWER partnership and the WPE Global Practice, translating core standards into partnership contexts and carrying partnership-generated practice back into the core.
- Support the sequencing of prevention and social norms activities to context, so they are introduced only where women-led community analysis confirms the preconditions for safe implementation are met.
- Maintain coherence of approach across the six countries without flattening contextual difference, identifying where a shared standard applies and where local adaptation is warranted.
- Track and report on delivery against scope, timeline, and budget across the six country programs, flagging deviation early enough for adaptive management rather than end-of-cycle correction.
- Ensure MEAL and program data feed directly into program adaptation, so that what the data shows changes what the program does, not only what it reports.
- Connect program data and implementation evidence to wider sector trends and debates, including comparable protection and GBV programming elsewhere.

**Learning, evidence, and the partnership learning agenda**

The role leads the program's learning function, treating implementation learning as a legitimate evidence pathway rather than a lesser substitute for external research. It also support the partnership’s advocacy pillar, so that evidence generated with the partners informs partners’ own advocacy and IRC’s policy positioning.

- Lead the design and delivery of the partnership learning pillar, coordinating cross-country learning cycles, documentation, and structured reflection between IRC and partners.
- Position women-led safety audits as community-generated risk analysis, and strengthen the pathway from that analysis into local decision-making and adaptive management.
- Build the program's evidence base on what enables and constrains change in protracted crisis settings, surfacing failure modes honestly, including referral systems that exist on paper but not in practice, and norms work that shifts survey scores without shifting community behavior.
- Ensure learning is co-owned with partners and feeds their own institutional positioning, not only IRC's reporting obligations.
- Steward the POWER advocacy pillar, supporting partners to carry community-generated analysis into local, national, and global advocacy where they hold standing in their own right.
- Work with advocacy and policy colleagues so the partnership's evidence informs IRC positioning toward donors, multilaterals, and normative bodies.

**Strengthening the core and surge capacity of women-led and local organizations**

The role supports partners on two distinct fronts, their institutional core and their capacity to surge in emergencies, resisting the pattern where localization language coexists with authority still held by the international actor.

- Support partner institutional strengthening across governance, financial systems, safeguarding, and MEAL in ways partners define and lead, consistent with the PEERS principles and the direct funding commitment.
- Strengthen partner surge and emergency response readiness under the emergency response pillar, so local organizations hold a credible role when crises escalate rather than being displaced by international surge.
- Advance the shift of analytical and decision-making authority toward partners with genuine institutional standing, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya, co-designing tools and thresholds with them rather than imposing them.
- Support the broader civil society and women's movement ecosystem the partnership connects to, recognizing partners as governance and coordination actors in their own right.

**Strategic focus on women and girls in conflict settings**

The role keeps women and girls in active conflict and protracted displacement at the center of the partnership, including where conflict-related sexual violence is a feature of the context.

- Ensure program design and adaptation are anchored in the realities faced by women and girls across the six contexts, several of which are shaped by active conflict and large-scale displacement.
- Support conflict-related sexual violence sensitive practice where relevant, including safe and consent-based documentation, clinical pathways, and Do No Harm decisions taken at closest proximity to violence, with pattern awareness fed upward.
- Keep adolescent girls visible as a distinct group rather than folded into a general women-and-girls category.

**Partnership and donor relationship management**

The role supports coherence of technical delivery across countries and reporting cycles, contributing technical content into the strategic relationship with Irish Aid, which AMU stewards and holds overall.

- Serve as a central program coordination point for the POWER partnership, supporting planning, adaptive management, amendments, and quality reporting to Irish Aid in coordination with the European DE & Frameworks team (Irish Aid).
- Feed technical content on program direction, learning, and strategic opportunities into AMU's communication with Irish Aid and the Department of Foreign Affairs. .
- Coordinate across the six country teams and the relevant IRC technical, advocacy, awards, and finance functions to keep the partnership coherent and its commitments met.
- Contribute technical input to AMU's design and negotiation of the next Strategic Partnership phase (post-2027), including program scope, theory of change, and the monitoring, evaluation and learning framework, coordinating input from WPE pillar leads, country teams, and partners, under AMU's overall lead on negotiation, timeline, and the donor relationship.

**Key working relationships**

**Works closely with:** AMU, Global and VPRU Advocacy; VPRU MEAL/METAL Unit.

Country WPE and program leads across the six POWER countries; POWER women-led and local partners, including SSWC in Somalia and FODDAJ in Kenya; IRC Awards Management Unit (AMU); VPRU Business Development; Irish Aid and Department of Foreign Affairs counterparts.

**Job requirements**

**Education:** Advanced degree in a relevant field such as social work, gender studies, international development, human rights, public health, or law, or an equivalent combination of qualification and experience.

**Work experience:** A minimum of 8 years professional experience in GBV, WPE, or protection programming in humanitarian and conflict-affected settings, at a technical lead level, including demonstrated experience in partnership and locally-led social action, in program quality or learning, and in program or grant management including budget oversight.

**Demonstrated skills and competencies:**

- Strong technical grounding in WPE practice and the IASC GBV Minimum Standards.
- Practical experience in feminist partnership and localization, including working with women-led organizations as partners rather than subgrantees.
- Learning and MEAL capability, with the judgment to treat implementation learning as evidence and to surface difficult findings.
- Program and grant management across multiple countries, including tracking and reporting r delivery against scope, timeline, and budget, and the systems to flag deviation early.
- Ability to translate program evidence into policy-relevant framing for donors, multilaterals, and normative processes.
- Multi-country coordination across diverse and often insecure contexts, with contextual and political sensitivity.
- Sound Do No Harm and safeguarding judgment, particularly in conflict-related sexual violence contexts.

**Languages:** Fluent English required. French is an asset given the East and Central Africa footprint, and Arabic is an asset for the Sudan and South Sudan contexts.

**Working environment and travel:** Possible travel across the six countries, including to hardship and conflict-affected locations.

***This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Kenya, Uganda, Burundi.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Palestine - Program Coordinator (M/F) - Jerusalem
body:
## About us

**Desired start date: 15/10/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 12 months**  
**Location: Jerusalem**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## La mission

In response to the attacks of 7 October 2023, the Israeli army launched a massive offensive in the Gaza Strip, beginning with a campaign of air strikes followed by a series of ground offensives that successively hit all the enclave's governorates. The intensity of the fighting, repeated strikes and successive evacuation orders have forced more than 1.7 million people to move, sometimes several times, to sites less directly affected by the fighting. The first displacements towards the south of Gaza, and more particularly the governorate of Rafah where 1.7 million Palestinians were displaced in April 2024, were followed by the displacement of more than 1 million people towards the central part of the Gaza Strip when the offensive on Rafah was launched in May 2024.

Displaced people are living in schools, organised sites and informal sites where it is more difficult to organise assistance. The destruction by the fighting of vital infrastructure, such as health facilities, water and electricity supplies, schools and other public services, is having a major impact on the displaced and host populations.

**SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONA**L teams have been working in Gaza since February 2024. Activities are currently being developed in the governorate of Deir el-Balah, in the centre of the Gaza Strip, where a base was opened in March.  
SI teams are implementing WASH activities, which include the installation and rehabilitation of water desalination plants to ensure the production of drinking water, the transport of water to displacement sites by tanker truck, and activities aimed at reducing health risks and improving the living conditions of displaced people through hygiene promotion sessions and the distribution of hygiene kits.

## Job description

**General objective:**

The Program Coordinator oversees the development and quality of SI’s programs, ensuring they are needs-driven, context-adapted, and impactful. S/He supports strategic planning, program monitoring, technical compliance, and coordination across teams, partners, and donors, while strengthening staff capacities and safeguarding ethical standards.

**The main challenges:**

1\) Developing strategy and defining SI value add for West Bank, including positioning on coordination architecture, and preparedness in the case of a medium-scale escalation.  
2\) Developing SI strategy and relevance in Shelter and FSL for Gaza.   
3\) Challenges include compliance, resource allocation, staff capacity, and integrating cross-cutting themes while mitigating operational and ethical risks.

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

Support the structuration of the mission, including onboarding new staff, expanding activities, and developing new sectors and areas of intervention.   
Reinforce quality monitoring of program strategies and ensure the implementation and harmonization of SI’s frameworks, tools, and procedures across all teams.  
Implement the strategy of the mission and develop the activities of SI in the West Bank   
Continue to support the activities and Gaza to kept Gaza as a key Wash actor

**Security constraints:**

The mission faces no particular security constraints in Jerusalem, however, there are major security and access challenges in the Gaza Strip.

## Votre profil

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

Master's degree in Humanitarian Action, human rights, social science (geography, sociology, anthropology, history) or Political Science is more preferable.

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 5 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1\) Program strategy development

2\) Multi-sector program design (WASH, FSL ).

3\) Partnership development and coordination

4)External coordination: engagement with clusters, international partners, and national actors

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1)Leadership and team management

2)Coordination across multi-level teams

3)Capacity building and training

**LANGUAGES**

**- English**

**- Arabic is an asset**

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

To date, SI have a coordination office and a guesthouse in Jerusalem. The office is fully furnished, and the guesthouse is equipped with all necessary equipment (internet, kitchen, laundry facilities, living room, etc.). Jerusalem is generally very safe, and staff can move freely across most areas of East and West Jerusalem. Walking is permitted.

title: Employment Specialist
body:
**Job Overview:**

The Employment Specialist helps newly arrived refugee clients achieve self-sufficiency through employment. This role delivers job readiness services, career coaching, and employer connections while supporting clients through the application and placement process. The Specialist maintains strong relationships with local employers, coordinates with other IRC staff, and ensures compliance with donor and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake and assessment for employment-eligible clients and develop individualized employment plans.
- Deliver job readiness orientations in both group and one-on-one settings, focusing on essential skills for employability.
- Cultivate and maintain relationships with area employers to identify appropriate opportunities for clients.
- Match clients to employment opportunities and guide them through applications, interviews, and hiring processes.
- Monitor job placements, wages, and satisfaction of both clients and employers, providing post-placement support.
- Assist clients with Unemployment Insurance applications and weekly claims when applicable.
